    • Say how many and when. Choose the weight between titles. Read the card carefully.
    • Confirm the mix favours the UK and Head of titles unless there is a reason not to.

    Every Step

    1. Type: "Plan the next wave for the [WEBINAR DATE] webinar."
    2. Check the card: broadcast id and date match, count is as asked, V2 is weighted up, excluded countries are excluded.
    3. Check the schedule is 3 to 7 days before the event, in UK time.
    4. Do not reply "send now" yet. First check the pool, the suppression sweep (3.4) and the configuration (2.5) are all done.

    Done When A wave plan the operator has read and could defend line by line.

    #TitleHistorical result across webinars 1 to 9 (evidence in 27.4)
    V1The Insider Roadmap to Access Top UK Fintech Board Seats in 2026Most used (about 110,000 invites)
    V2The Strategic Framework to Stop Advising and Start Governing in 2026Best: 0.636%, 1.17 times the base
    V3The Governance Blueprint to Master Risk and Secure Board Roles in 2026Below average: 0.331%
    V4The Credibility Model to Transition from Executive to Director in 2026Below average: 0.405%
    V5Inside the Boardroom: A Framework for Fintech Board Roles in 2026Small sample

    The five titles are canonical and never renumbered. The invite body names what will be covered (what board-ready really means, how headhunters shortlist, SMCR exposure, AI governance oversight, portfolio career structure, red flags), is hosted by the operator, and ends: "No further updates will be sent." A decline is treated as an opt-out.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The plan lists why leads were skipped. A silent skip is not acceptable.
    • The invite title mix is deliberate, informed by the results table below.

    Common Mistakes

    • Skimming the card because the last wave was fine. The card changes when the date, pool or config changes.

    4.2 Send and Verify a Wave

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 30 minSystem TantraSafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    This step reaches people and cannot be taken back. It follows a strict order so that a failure never burns leads: create, wait, verify, and only then stamp the sheet.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • On "send now", creates each campaign with every required setting: balanced distribution, London time, attendee add delay of at least 15, the WebinarGeek broadcast linked, yes and maybe auto-registered, the location with its UTM tag, one variation tag.
    • Waits about 30 seconds, reads each campaign back, confirms creationStatus: ready, and marks only those leads as used.
    What the Operator Does
    • Type "send now" only after reading the plan.
    • Do not create waves by hand-built API calls. The create-only fields can never be fixed afterwards.

    Every Step

    1. Reply: "send now".
    2. Wait for the verification line for each wave.
    3. If a wave is not ready, re-check after a few minutes. Do not re-send.
    4. Do not judge the wave today. Delivery truth comes from the calendar RSVPs and the next day's dashboard.

    Done When Every wave reads ready, and the sheet is stamped for those waves only.

    Why Stamp Last

    The old rule stamped the sheet before the campaign was created, to avoid an unrecorded send. That reversed on 6 August: a stamp means consumed, so stamping a wave that then fails to create burns those leads permanently. Stamping is now done by Claude through the connector, per row, after verification.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Only waves that verified ready are stamped.
    • If staggered timing is wanted, say so in the plan: the connector's send tool takes one UTC time per chunk and Tantra lands the invites near that time. Rows are still stamped at creation.

    Common Mistakes

    • Re-running a wave that looked slow. It sends twice.
    • Using the generic Tantra create-campaign tool. It cannot set the broadcast link or auto-register, so the campaign is misconfigured for good.

    4.3 Launch the Cold Email (Instantly)

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 1 hourSystem InstantlySafety Go

    Why It Matters

    The same three-step sequence is reused for every webinar with the date swapped, so the risk is not writing the email. The risk is a stale date left in one step, a lead list that includes people who asked to be removed, or a campaign that starts before anyone checked it.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Lists campaigns (ids change every webinar), reads the latest in full, and proposes the date and time replacements as a plan card.
    • On "go", copies it into a new draft and refuses if any old date or time is left in the copy.
    • Previews leads with suppressed, blocked and previously contacted people removed, then loads them in batches on "go".
    • Edits any step (subject, body, delay), the name, daily limit or end date, showing the exact before and after.
    What the Operator Does
    • Review the draft together with Claude.
    • Reply "send now" for the exact preview, and only then is the campaign activated.

    Every Step

    1. Type: "Set up the Instantly campaign for the [WEBINAR DATE] webinar."
    2. Read the date replacements. Check the name will be Webinar <n> - <D Month>.
    3. Reply "go". Claude creates the draft.
    4. Review the three steps (see the sequence below). Ask for any edit by typing it, for example: "Change the first subject and replace [OLD DATE] with [WEBINAR DATE]."
    5. Preview the leads. Reply "go" to load them.
    6. Check the campaign status in Instantly. Start it only with "send now".

    Done When A dated draft with clean leads loaded, checked, and started only on "send now".

    The Three Steps (Abridged)

    1. "Someone less qualified just got that board seat. Here is why." Two equal candidates, one gets the seat. The difference is knowing how board searches run behind closed doors.
    2. "The part of board searches nobody talks about." Many appointments are filled before a post goes live, through headhunter shortlists, referrals and nominations.
    3. "Are you looking to join a Fintech Board?" A short reminder with an offer to be removed from the list.

    Signed with the sending account name and FINTECH Circle. The estate is eleven domains and fifty mailboxes, eight of the domains sending through a third-party provider.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The status field is read, never the name. A campaign called DRAFT can be active.
    • The retarget campaign aims at the previous webinar's yes and maybe no-shows.

    Common Mistakes

    • Reusing a list that bounced badly. Webinar 7 reached 12.8% and the June re-marketing list 35%.
    • Quoting Instantly's reply count. It under-reports about forty-four times, and open tracking is off.

    4.4 Send Warm Re-Invites

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 30 minSystem Tantra, InstantlySafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    People who registered for a past webinar but never attended, and who are not customers or opted out, convert several times better than cold leads. They already know the offer. It is the cheapest traffic the funnel has.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Builds the audience from WebinarGeek, not GHL tags: past registrants minus attendees minus customers minus anyone suppressed.
    • Plans it as a wave or an Instantly campaign with the same safety levels as cold outreach.
    What the Operator Does
    • Choose the message. A short note referring to the replay works better than a repeat of the cold invite.
    • Confirm the audience size before sending.

    Every Step

    1. Type: "Build a warm re-invite audience for [WEBINAR DATE] from past no-shows."
    2. Read the audience count and the exclusions.
    3. Plan and send as in 4.1 and 4.2, or as in 4.3 for email.

    Done When A warm re-invite audience is plan-carded, sent and verified.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The audience comes from WebinarGeek attendance. GHL's watched-false tag is not a no-show list.
    • The first dedicated batch ran in September 2026 (historical; see the Event Log, webinar 10).

    Common Mistakes

    • Including attendees or customers. A past attendee invited again is a signal to unsubscribe.

    4.5 Fix or Cancel a Wave

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 10 minSystem TantraSafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    A wave with a wrong date, wrong title or wrong audience is the most damaging error the funnel can make, and it must be handled the minute it is noticed. Cancelling stops invites that are still scheduled. It cannot recall invites that were already delivered.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reports first whether the invites are still scheduled, which cancelling should stop, or already delivered, which it cannot.
    • Cancels the wave on "send now" and leaves the leads stamped as used.
    What the Operator Does
    • Say exactly what is wrong and what the corrected wave should be.

    Every Step

    1. Type: "Cancel the wave scheduled for tomorrow and plan a corrected one."
    2. Read the delivered or scheduled report.
    3. Reply "send now" to cancel.
    4. Plan the corrected wave as in 4.1. Only name and tags can be edited on an existing campaign; anything else is cancel and recreate.

    Done When The wrong wave is stopped or accounted for, and a correct plan exists.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Corrections for already delivered invites are planned as a separate message, not hidden.

    Common Mistakes

    • Editing the time after invites went out. Invites already sent keep the old time.

    4.6 Set Up LinkedIn Retargeting

    Owner Operations, OperatorTime 1 hourSystem LinkedIn Campaign ManagerSafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    Everyone who was emailed or invited can also see FINTECH Circle content on LinkedIn, but organic posts cannot be targeted at a list. Ads can. A matched audience built from past webinar contacts reaches the same people a second time, in a different place, without more email volume.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Builds the contact list from the contacted-people history, with suppressed people and blocked domains removed, and writes the file in LinkedIn's upload format.
    • Reports the audience size and flags any exclusion.
    What the Operator Does
    • Create the matched audience in Campaign Manager: Account Assets, Matched Audiences, Create, Upload a list. Plan for a minimum of 300 matched LinkedIn members, counted after LinkedIn matches the list and not by rows in the file, and for 24 to 48 hours of processing, sometimes longer for large lists. Confirm these figures in Campaign Manager before the launch date is fixed.
    • Agree the ad creative first. The best organic posts are the creative.

    Every Step

    1. Run the suppression sweep (3.4). Blocked domains and opted-out people must not be uploaded.
    2. Ask the chat for the list: "Build the LinkedIn upload file from all past webinar contacts, excluding opt-outs and blocked domains."
    3. Show the plan card. An upload reaches people, so it needs "send now".
    4. Upload in Campaign Manager. Wait for matching to finish.
    5. Launch a small test ad using a top organic post (5.7), and read the result before scaling.

    Done When A matched audience exists, excluding everyone suppressed, with a test ad running to it.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The audience comes from the contacted history, not one sheet tab. Early tabs show who was targeted, not who was sent.
    • The ads promote posts that have already worked organically.

    Common Mistakes

    • Writing ad creative from scratch. The posts decide which creative works.

    4.7 Read the Outreach at Day 3 to 4

    Owner Operations, OperatorTime 15 minSystem Dashboard, calendar RSVPsSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    RSVPs accrue over days. A wave that looks flat on day 1 is not failing, and a wave that looks strong on day 1 has not won. Judging early leads to panic changes that harm a good wave.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the yes, maybe, no and waiting counts from the calendar RSVPs for each campaign, never Tantra's sent counter.
    • Compares to the same point in earlier webinars.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide whether a second wave is needed, and in which segments.

    Every Step

    1. On day 3 or 4, type: "How many yes or maybe so far, by campaign and by invite title?"
    2. Compare to the last webinar at the same distance from the event.
    3. If more registrations are needed, plan the next wave (4.1) weighted toward the segments that are winning.

    Done When A read, with the time it was taken, and a decision to send more or hold.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Every figure carries the time it was read.
    • Segments are compared on the full history and not on one wave.

    Common Mistakes

    • Reading Tantra's sentCount. It is zero for calendar campaigns that did send.

    4.8 Know the Limits of Every Channel

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 10 minSystem Tantra, Instantly, LinkedInSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Current Going over a channel's limits loses the asset, not just the campaign: a burned sending domain, a restricted LinkedIn account, a wasted ad budget. Every channel has a safe daily pace, and the pace changes with how old and how warm the sender is. The reference playbooks give conservative starting points for a brand-new sender. FINTECH's own planning figures are higher, and the two must not be mixed up.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the live sender settings through the connector's sender tool, so the real per-mailbox limits are shown, not remembered.
    • Works out how many people a plan can reach from the mailboxes, their daily limit and the days available, and says which limit binds first.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide the safe pace for each new sender. Where the reference and FINTECH's figures differ, the more cautious number applies to anything new.
    • Add mailboxes or start earlier when the list is bigger than the capacity. Never raise a limit to catch up.

    Every Step

    1. Ask: "How many people can the senders reach before the [WEBINAR DATE] webinar, and which limit binds first?"
    2. Read the answer against the table below.
    3. If the list is bigger than the capacity, add senders or start earlier. Do not push one sender harder.
    4. Scale in steps. A sudden jump in volume is the clearest signal a spam filter reads.

    Done When The plan fits inside every limit, and the limit that binds first is named.

    ChannelReference starting pointFINTECH planning figureWhat breaks if ignored
    Calendar invites20 a day per cold mailbox, 50 once warmed, never above 200. SPF, DKIM and DMARC first. Outreach domains only.About 250 per mailbox a day; about 1,500 per service account a day (the shared quota)The domain, permanently
    Cold email20 a day while warming, 50 once warm. 2 to 3 weeks of warm-up. List bounce below 1%. Reject a bought list above 2% duplicates.50 mailboxes across 11 domains. Bounce is tracked per campaign.Inbox placement for every domain
    LinkedIn outreachAbout 15 to 20 connection requests a day per account to start; the reference also plans up to 200 a week. LinkedIn publishes no exact limits.Not run todayThe account, with no appeal
    Paid adsSmallest viable budget first. One variable per test. Retargeting pool live from day one.LinkedIn retargeting onlyBudget, fastest of all
    Blog and socialNo daily limit. One post per profile per day is the ceiling.Content engine (Part 5)Nothing breaks; quality drifts
    The Send Timing Differs

    The reference sends a dated event's whole list 8 to 12 days before. FINTECH's own evidence says 3 to 7 days before, judged at day 3 to 4. FINTECH's timing is the one in use and it stays.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The shared Google quota is named as the real limit for calendar invites: about 1,500 invites per service account per day, against a headline of about 5,000 for 20 mailboxes.
    • New senders follow the reference pace until they have proven themselves.

    Common Mistakes

    • Planning to the headline of 5,000 a day when the shared quota allows far less.
    • Using FINTECH's 250 a day figure for a mailbox that has not warmed.

    4.9 Run the Weekly Scale, Hold or Fix Gate

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 20 minSystem Instantly, dashboardSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Available Every week each cold email inbox and campaign gets one verdict: scale it, hold it, or fix it. The verdict names the cause, so the fix goes to the right place: a deliverability problem needs the inbox stopped, a message problem needs a new offer. The thresholds below are reference starting points, to be replaced with FINTECH's own once enough weeks have been read.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads each campaign's click-through, conversion and bounce rate from Instantly and the dashboard.
    • Applies the gate and names the verdict and the cause, with the numbers and the time they were read.
    What the Operator Does
    • Agree the starting points, then change them as FINTECH's own history grows.
    • Approve any pause or stop. Pausing an inbox reaches live sending.

    Every Step

    1. Type: "Run the weekly cold email gate for last week."
    2. Read the verdict for each campaign and each inbox.
    3. Act on fixes first: stop a failing inbox the same day.
    4. Scale only what passes all three scale tests, and add budget or mailboxes, not new variables.

    Done When Each campaign has one verdict and one cause, recorded with the time it was read.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Bounce above the stop line pauses the inbox today, before the verdict is discussed.
    • The verdict separates a deliverability problem from a message problem.

    Common Mistakes

    • Reading open rate. Open tracking is off at FINTECH, so the open-rate test cannot be applied and is skipped.
    • Scaling on one good week.

    4.10 Write the Calendar Invite

    Owner Operator, ClaudeTime 30 minSystem TantraSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Current The invite description is the only copy the recipient reads. Keep it short, make the promise first, and make declining easy. FINTECH already follows several of these rules: five canonical titles, no first-name placeholders, the location rule and a closing line. The checklist below adds the rest, taken from the reference playbooks.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Checks a draft title and description against the rules below and lists every breach.
    • Keeps the approved text, then checks the live campaign against it after creation.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve the final text. The same text goes to every guest, so it is read once and read carefully.

    Every Step

    1. Draft or paste the title and description.
    2. Ask: "Check this invite against the copy rules."
    3. Fix every breach. Approve the final text.
    4. After the wave is created, ask Claude to compare the live campaign with the approved text.

    Done When The approved text matches the live campaign word for word.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The title reads like a meeting, with the topic and the outcome. No $, % or the word free.
    • The first lines say who it is for and what they leave with. The date, time and time zone come first, so the invite never promises a different time from the event platform.
    • One line makes declining easy, so fewer people report the invite.

    Common Mistakes

    • A long description that buries the promise below the calendar preview.
    • A first name in the title or text. The text is identical for every guest.
    • Replacing FINTECH's location tag with the reference tag. FINTECH keeps ?utm_source=cal.

    4.11 Set Up a Calendar Sender in Tantra

    Owner OperationsTime 30 min per senderSystem Google Admin, TantraSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Current The 20 calendar senders are already connected and warmed. This card applies when a sender is added or replaced. A sender is one mailbox that Tantra may act for. Getting it wrong either leaves the sender disconnected or sends too much from a cold mailbox.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the senders through the connector's sender tool: which are connected, their daily limit and whether each is marked cold or warmed.
    • Reports any sender left on a default limit.
    What the Operator Does
    • In Google Admin, give Tantra's service account permission to act for the mailboxes. This step cannot be done by Claude.
    • In Tantra, verify and add the senders, then set each one's daily guests and warm status.

    Every Step

    1. Upload the service account key in Tantra. Nothing can send until this is done.
    2. In Google Admin, add the permissions in the table below. It can take minutes, and occasionally up to an hour, to take effect.
    3. In Tantra, verify and add the sender addresses. Each should show Connected. If one shows Disconnected, wait a few minutes and re-authenticate.
    4. Set the guests per day: 20 while the inbox is cold, 50 once it has warmed for 2 to 3 weeks. Set the Warm flag to Cold or Warmed to match.
    5. Ask Claude to read the senders back and confirm no default was left in place.

    Done When Every new sender shows Connected, with a guests-per-day figure and a warm flag that match its age.

    PermissionIn plain words
    CalendarSee and create calendar events as the mailbox.
    Calendar eventsAdd guests to those events, so the invite goes out.
    Send mailSend mail as the mailbox. Needed for the welcome and cold email sends.
    Email address and profileKnow whose mailbox it is, so the right name shows on the invite.
    Mailbox changes (cold email in Tantra only)Tell a real reply from an automatic one. Without it the sender shows as calendar-only.
    Read mail (only for the reader in 4.12)Read replies and bounce notices so they can be recorded.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Never leave the default limit in place.
    • Several senders share the volume, each inside its own daily limit.
    • FINTECH's calendar service account is set up for calendar access only. Adding mailbox access is a separate decision.

    Common Mistakes

    • Pasting the service account's email where the numeric client number is wanted.
    • Setting Warmed on an inbox that has not warmed, which allows a pace the domain cannot carry.

    4.12 Read RSVPs and Bounces Automatically

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime Build onceSystem Sender mailboxes, Tantra, sheetSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Available Replies to calendar invites land in the 20 sender mailboxes and a person does not read them. The reader handles the one reply that matters most: a reply of stop or unsubscribe moves the person onto Tantra's unsubscribe list automatically (being wired now). It can also record accepted, tentative and declined answers and put bounces on the do-not-contact list. FINTECH already reads RSVP counts from the sender calendars; the reader would add the replies and bounces that calendars do not show.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Checks the sender mailboxes every 60 seconds. A failed delivery marks the person bounced and adds them to the do-not-contact tab.
    • Otherwise reads the calendar reply: accepted is yes, tentative is maybe, declined is no, and records it on the contact.
    • Never registers anyone. Registration already comes from the webinar linked to the campaign.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve the build and the extra read-only mailbox permission (see 4.11).
    • Check a test run on three sample messages before it goes live.

    Every Step

    1. Decide where the answers are recorded: the contact record and the do-not-contact tab (3.6).
    2. Add the read-only mailbox permission for the sender mailboxes.
    3. Ask Claude to build the reader and show a test run on three sample messages.
    4. Approve it, then check the first day's bounces against the tab.

    Done When A reply, a bounce and an opt-out each show on the right record within a few minutes.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Each message is processed once. Anything already read is skipped.
    • A decline is treated as an opt-out, as FINTECH already does.

    Common Mistakes

    • Letting the reader register people. It would double-register them.
    • Giving it more mailbox access than reading.

    4.13 Tag Every Link So Registrations Can Be Traced

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 15 minSystem Registration page, dashboardSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Available Without a tag on every link, a registration cannot be traced to a channel, and a channel cannot be judged. FINTECH already tags the invite location with ?utm_source=cal. The full schema adds a medium, a campaign and a content tag, so each webinar, each channel and each variant has its own row.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Builds each link with the same four parts and checks every link before a send.
    • Reads the registrations by source from the dashboard and reports per run and per source.
    • Excludes test contacts from every count (3.8).
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve the tag names once. Keep them lowercase and never rename them mid-campaign.

    Every Step

    1. Agree the four parts: source, medium, campaign, content.
    2. Ask Claude to apply them to every link in the next wave, the email steps and the ads.
    3. Ask: "Show registrations by source for the last webinar."
    4. Compare channels on the same page and the same time window.

    Done When Every registration for the webinar names a source, and no test contact is counted.

    What Good Looks Like

    • One row per run and per source, so channels compare fairly.
    • The content tag names the variant or the post, so winners can be repeated.

    Common Mistakes

    • Changing tag spelling halfway, which splits one channel into two rows.
    • Counting a test registration as a real one.

    4.14 Rank Channels by Cost per Buyer

    Owner Operator, ClaudeTime 30 min a monthSystem Dashboard, GA4Safety Read

    Why It Matters

    Available Registrations are not buyers, and clicks are not registrations. The only fair comparison across channels is the cost per buyer: what a channel cost, divided by the buyers it brought. Once a month the channels are ranked, and some budget moves from the dearest towards the cheapest, keeping total spend the same. The figures in the pictures are an illustration of the method, not FINTECH results.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads spend per channel, registrations by source and buyers, and divides.
    • Ranks the channels and proposes a budget move, with the numbers.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve any budget move. It spends or stops spending money.

    Every Step

    1. Ask: "Rank the channels by cost per buyer for last month."
    2. Read the ranking. Check each channel has enough buyers to mean anything.
    3. Move budget from the most expensive channel towards the cheapest, keeping the total the same.
    4. Leave a small test budget on every channel, so a channel that gets cheap again is noticed.

    Done When A ranked list, a budget move decided, and a small test budget kept on every channel.

    What Good Looks Like

    • A channel with only one or two buyers is flagged as a weak signal, not ranked firmly.
    • Paid media spend is compared with organic channels on the same page and window.

    Common Mistakes

    • Cutting a channel to zero. Nothing then shows when it gets cheap again.
    • Ranking by cost per registration, which hides channels that register many and buy none.

    4.15 Run Meta Paid Ads

    Owner Operator, Operations, ClaudeTime Half a day to set upSystem Meta Ads Manager, pixelSafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    Available Meta ads are not run by FINTECH today. They are the way to buy traffic beyond the contact list, and they burn money fastest of any channel. So the rule is: track the registration first, test two ads on a small budget, and scale only what converts. Everything is built paused, and a person switches it on.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Checks the pixel is on the pages and that each registration is also sent to Meta from the server (the conversions API), so tracking survives browsers that block it.
    • Builds the retargeting pool, a registrants audience and, once enough people have registered, a lookalike.
    • Builds the campaign, the ad set and two ads, all paused, and reads the weekly cost per registration.
    What the Operator Does
    • Create the business account, the ad account with a payment method, the page and the pixel if any are missing.
    • Set the target cost per registration and the small daily budget.
    • Switch the campaign on in Ads Manager. Claude never does.

    Every Step

    1. Make the registration the conversion, in Google Analytics and in Meta. Reuse the existing registration event (4.22). Do not create a second one.
    2. Install the pixel and send each registration to Meta from the server as well.
    3. Start the retargeting pool before any ad runs: visitors of the last 30 days who did not register.
    4. Exclude registrants from the pool and the targeting, so nobody is paid for twice.
    5. Build the lookalike once 100 people have registered.
    6. Write two ads that differ only in angle: one benefit-led, one problem-led. Same image style, page and audience.
    7. Launch on a small fixed budget. Change one variable per test.
    8. Judge each ad weekly by cost per registration against the target.

    Done When Both ads are live with tagged links, a test registration shows in Meta and Google Analytics, and the target cost per registration is written down.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The pool exists before the first ad runs, so early visitors are not lost.
    • Only one thing changes per test: never the budget and the creative in the same week.

    Common Mistakes

    • Judging ads by clicks instead of cost per registration.
    • Launching before a test registration shows in Meta and Google Analytics.
    • Building the pool after the first ads run.

    4.16 Sync LinkedIn Lead Forms to Registration

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 1 hour plus the review waitSystem LinkedIn Campaign Manager, funnelSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Available A LinkedIn lead form lets someone register without leaving LinkedIn. The sign-up then stays inside Campaign Manager unless something carries it over, and nobody confirms it or reminds that person. A small sync reads each new sign-up every 10 minutes and registers it on the funnel, tagged as LinkedIn, so the person gets the same confirmation and reminders as anyone else.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads new sign-ups from the lead forms every 10 minutes and registers each one, tagged as LinkedIn.
    • Only reads leads. It never changes a campaign.
    What the Operator Does
    • Request the lead sync access on the LinkedIn developer app and wait for LinkedIn's review. This is the slow part, so request it first.
    • Create the access token with the two read permissions and paste it with the ad account number.
    • Renew the token before it expires. It lasts 60 days.

    Every Step

    1. Request lead sync access on the LinkedIn app today. LinkedIn reviews it first.
    2. When approved, create the token with the two read permissions: lead retrieval and ads reading.
    3. Give Claude the token and the ad account number (the number after accounts in the Campaign Manager address).
    4. Put the token expiry in the calendar, for example a reminder at day 50.
    5. Submit a test form and confirm the person is registered within 10 minutes.

    Done When A test form sign-up appears as a registered contact, tagged LinkedIn, within 10 minutes.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The 60-day expiry has a reminder well before it. A lapsed token stops new leads silently.
    • Both permissions are ticked. With one missing the sync cannot read the leads.

    Common Mistakes

    • Creating the token before LinkedIn approves the access.
    • Pasting the whole address instead of the account number.

    4.17 Run LinkedIn Outreach

    Owner Operator, OperationsTime 2 hours to buildSystem Tantra, LinkedInSafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    Available LinkedIn outreach reaches named buyers through one real profile. FINTECH does not run it today. It must be paced, because LinkedIn restricts accounts that send too fast and publishes no exact limits. A campaign sends a short note, then five follow-ups only to people who accept.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Imports the clean list of people with a LinkedIn address and builds the campaign paused, with the note in two versions and five follow-ups.
    • Trims the note to 300 characters and tags every link as LinkedIn.
    • Reads the numbers each day: requests sent, accepted and replied.
    What the Operator Does
    • Connect the LinkedIn profile by hand inside Tantra. Sign-in is the one step nobody can do on the operator's behalf.
    • Approve every message and the start.
    • Withdraw unaccepted requests after 14 days.

    Every Step

    1. Connect the profile. It needs a photo, a real headline and a real network. No other LinkedIn automation tool may run on the same profile.
    2. Start at about 15 to 20 connection requests a day per account. Limits apply per account across every campaign.
    3. Write a note of at most 300 characters in two versions: one leads with the outcome, one with the objection.
    4. After a person accepts, five messages go out at 0, 3, 7, 12 and 25 days.
    5. Leave a request open for up to 14 days, then withdraw it.
    6. Once a request is withdrawn, LinkedIn blocks a new request to that person for three weeks. Do not re-request inside that window.
    7. Raise the pace a little each week only while acceptance stays healthy. If LinkedIn shows a warning, drop back.

    Done When The campaign runs at a safe pace, every link is tagged LinkedIn, and LinkedIn registrations show with that source.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Only people who accept are messaged. Everyone else is left alone.
    • One campaign per sender, so each carries one voice.
    • A free account can add a note to only about 5 to 10 requests a month; after that requests go without a note.

    Common Mistakes

    • Running another automation tool on the same profile.
    • Counting hours instead of days for the accept window, so late accepters never get a message.

    4.18 Publish a LinkedIn Event Page

    Owner OperatorTime 30 minSystem LinkedIn company pageSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Available A company event gives LinkedIn a second, free path to the registration page. It is not automated: a person creates it. The event drives clicks; the registration itself happens on FINTECH's own page. Because the registration is external, LinkedIn gives no attendee list, so the count comes from the registration page.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the event post text and the tagged link.
    • Counts LinkedIn registrations by filtering the registrations to the LinkedIn source.
    What the Operator Does
    • Create the event on the company page, as an admin, on a computer.
    • Invite the profile's own first-degree connections in daily batches.

    Every Step

    1. Open the company page as a super admin or content admin: Admin view, Create, Create an event.
    2. Set the format to an external event link.
    3. Match the name, date, time and time zone to the webinar exactly. The organizer, event type and format cannot be changed after the event is created.
    4. Upload the banner and set the external registration link to the page with the LinkedIn tag on the end.
    5. Write the post text and post it.
    6. Open the event and invite connections in daily batches. Only the profile's own first-degree connections can be invited, and LinkedIn allows each page admin 1,000 invitations a week across all events.

    Done When The event is live, matches the webinar to the minute, and registrations carry the LinkedIn tag.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Date and time match the event platform to the minute.
    • Registrations are counted from the registration page, not from the event's attendee count.

    Common Mistakes

    • Reporting the event's own attendee count as registrations.
    • Changing the date on the event page but not on the webinar, or the reverse.

    4.19 Try a Five-Step Cold Email Thread

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 1 hourSystem InstantlySafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Potential FINTECH's cold email is a three-step sequence. The reference playbooks use a five-step thread on days 0, 3, 6, 9 and 13. Only the first step has a subject; steps 2 to 5 are short replies in the same thread. It could be tested against the three-step sequence, with one variable changed at a time.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the five steps with A and B versions and tags every link.
    • Checks the capacity: a five-step thread uses up to five sends per person.
    • Runs it as a separate campaign so it can be compared.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve the copy. Decide whether to test it.

    Every Step

    1. Decide the test: three steps against five, on the same list quality.
    2. Write five steps. Only step 1 has a subject. Put an unsubscribe line in every step.
    3. Use only the personal fields the tool fills. If a name is missing, drop it from the sentence.
    4. Send Monday to Friday in business hours in the audience's time zone.
    5. Read it at the weekly gate (4.9).

    Done When A five-step campaign runs beside the existing one, and the gate compares them.

    What Good Looks Like

    • A reply ends that person's thread. Test this by replying to a test message.
    • Capacity is checked first: five steps reaches a fifth as many people.

    Common Mistakes

    • Giving steps 2 to 5 their own subject lines, which breaks the thread.
    • Changing the offer and the length in the same test.

    4.20 Publish One Pillar Blog Post a Month

    Owner Operator, ClaudeTime 2 hours a monthSystem Website, GA4Safety Go

    Why It Matters

    Potential One long post a month, built on a question a buyer already asks, becomes a page that keeps earning and the source material for a month of social posts. FINTECH does not run a blog today. It is the one channel that compounds, and it is judged by one number: how many readers click through to the registration page.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Drafts the post from approved notes and flags every claim that needs a source.
    • Tags the call-to-action link with the blog source and the post's name.
    • Reads the clicks to the registration page each week and gives the verdict.
    What the Operator Does
    • Choose the topic from a real buyer pain.
    • Approve the post, then read it on a phone like a stranger.

    Every Step

    1. Pick one buyer pain and give the post a promise headline with a number.
    2. Claude drafts it. Delete anything it made up, especially numbers.
    3. Approve it. It goes live on the funnel's own pages.
    4. Check the date, the link with its tag, and that nothing is cut off on a phone.
    5. Each week divide clicks to the registration page by the post's views. At 3% or more, keep going. Under 1%, change the call to action.
    6. Hand the post to the social engine to cut into clips and quotes (Part 5).

    Done When The post is live, its link is tagged as blog, and a test click shows as blog traffic.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Read by source and medium, not by channel group, or the blog has no row of its own.
    • The call to action carries the session date and is refreshed before each new cycle.

    Common Mistakes

    • Judging by views. Engagement is not traffic.
    • An untagged link, so the post's registrations cannot be traced.

    4.21 Use SMS Sparingly

    Owner OperationsTime Setup waits on approvalSystem SMS senderSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Potential SMS is the most intrusive channel and the only one that reaches a phone's lock screen. The reference playbooks use it for time-critical moments only: a missed-call rebook, a go-live nudge, a rare nudge when something cannot wait. FINTECH uses email for reminders and WhatsApp for some messages, and does not run SMS. The setup has waits that cannot be shortened, such as sender verification and the carrier's regulatory review, so it is started early if it is wanted at all.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the message as one segment of 160 plain characters, with no emoji.
    • Sends only to people who have agreed to SMS, and respects every opt-out.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide whether SMS is wanted at all.
    • Approve the sender and the consent wording.

    Every Step

    1. Decide the one or two moments where an SMS earns its place.
    2. Start the sender verification and regulatory review early.
    3. Write each message as a single segment.
    4. Send only to people who consented. Keep SMS out of the weekly letter.

    Done When One approved sender, a consent record, and a message that fits one segment.

    What Good Looks Like

    • One segment, plain text, one link.
    • SMS is the exception, not a weekly habit.

    Common Mistakes

    • Adding SMS reminders on top of the funnel's own, so people get two of each.
    • Texting people who gave only an email address.

    4.22 Count Registrations as a GA4 Key Event

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 30 minSystem Google AnalyticsSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Available Everything in this part depends on being able to count registrations by source. Google Analytics does this with one event: the registration form submission, sent from the thank-you page and marked as a key event. Then one report shows registrations by source and medium, which feeds the monthly ranking (4.14) and the ad decisions (4.15).

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Checks that the registration event fires once on a test registration.
    • Reads the key events column by source and medium and reports it.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve adding the analytics tag to the pages if it is not there already.

    Every Step

    1. In Google Analytics, open the events list and find generate_lead.
    2. Turn on the star so it counts as a key event.
    3. Submit a test registration and confirm the event appears once in the real-time report. Standard reports can take up to 24 hours.
    4. Open Acquisition, Traffic acquisition. Change the first column to session source and medium and read the key events column.
    5. Tag test contacts so they never count (3.8).

    Done When A test registration shows once in the real-time report, and the key events column reads registrations by source.

    What Good Looks Like

    • One registration event only. A second event doubles every count.
    • Read by source and medium, not by channel group.

    Common Mistakes

    • Creating a second event for the same registration.
    • Reading the standard report within hours and thinking nothing arrived.

    The Lessons in This Section

    • Every wave is planned, then sent, then verified, in that order. Verification comes before stamping.
    • Calendar invites are the largest channel. The V2 title and the UK are the proven combination.
    • Warm re-invites are the cheapest traffic. Never include attendees or customers.
    • Judge at day 3 to 4. Never judge on day 1.
    • Reference limits are starting points for a new sender. FINTECH's own figures apply only to a warmed estate.
    • Every channel not yet run is badged Available or Potential, and a person approves anything that reaches people or spends money.
    Part 6

    Landing, Registration and Tracking

    One page, four places, and the rule that keeps email and WhatsApp from crossing.

    Master Playbook

    LeadTrafficLandingNurtureLiveAfter

    8 task cards1 sectionReviewed by Operator as runner

    Why One Page

    The registration page is the single destination for every invite, email, post and ad. Sending everything to one page keeps the system simple, even if some registrations are lost compared with one-click registration on LinkedIn. It also means a captured email is a work email, a phone number is captured, and every registration is tracked the same way.

    Where it lives. webinar.fintechcircle.com is a Cloudflare Worker named fintech-branded-lp in the team's own Cloudflare account. It is a static site. The registration backend is hosted by GrowthClub. Calendar invites link with ?utm_source=cal, lead-gen forms with ?utm_source=lg_form and ads with ?utm_source=linkedinad.

    The One Rule That Keeps It Untangled

    WebinarGeek owns email. GHL owns WhatsApp. A Cloudflare Worker is the only thing that writes between them. The two channels never cross, so nobody is messaged twice.

    6.1 Test a Registration End to End

    Owner OperationsTime 20 minSystem Landing page, WebinarGeek, GHLSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    The funnel can look healthy while the registration path is broken. A form that returns success but never reaches WebinarGeek costs real registrations silently. The only way to know the path works is to walk it.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the webinar's subscriber list, the Registrants tab and the GHL contact after the test, and reports which of the four places received it.
    What the Operator Does
    • Submit the test, with a fresh test email, in a private window.

    Every Step

    1. Open the page in a private window. Check the date shown.
    2. Submit a registration with a test email and a real phone the tester controls.
    3. Check a confirmation arrives from WebinarGeek.
    4. On the thank-you page, send the WhatsApp message "send me my join link". Check the join link arrives.
    5. Ask the chat: "Is the test registration in WebinarGeek, the Work Tracker and GHL, and which tags does it have?"
    6. Tag the test contact test and delete or label it, so it never counts as a real registration.

    Done When The test appears in all four places and the WhatsApp reply arrived.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Timezone agrees in two places: the page and the Worker both use Europe/London.
    • A fresh email address is used every time.

    Common Mistakes

    • Testing only the form's success message.

    6.2 Know the Registration Path

    Owner EveryoneTime 10 minSystem Landing page, WebinarGeek, GHL, WorkerSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    When something goes wrong at registration, knowing which of the four places failed saves hours. This card is the path written down, and the thing to read when a registrant says they never got their link.

    Every Step

    1. Read the path below.
    2. When a person reports a missing email, check WebinarGeek's subscriber list first. If they are not there, the registration failed and should be redone.
    3. When a person reports a missing WhatsApp reminder, check whether they gave a phone number, and whether they sent the join-link message. No message from them means no WhatsApp window.
    4. Check the state tags on the GHL contact: they show what the Worker last heard.

    Done When Any team member can say which system holds what for any registrant.

    The Path of One Registration

    1. The registration form sends one submit to four places at once: WebinarGeek (the only one that can fail the registration), a Google Sheet, GoHighLevel, and the thank-you page.
    2. WebinarGeek sends the confirmation immediately and the reminders on schedule.
    3. The thank-you page asks the registrant to WhatsApp "send me my join link". That inbound message opens WhatsApp's 24-hour window, which is why the confirmation can be a free-form message. This ask is load-bearing. Do not remove it.
    4. GoHighLevel replies with the join link, then sends four timed WhatsApp reminders anchored on the broadcast date. The morning reminder sits 4.5 hours before the broadcast.
    5. The Worker keeps GHL up to date from WebinarGeek events (registered, unsubscribed, watched live, watched replay, not watched, clicked the call to action) by setting state tags.
    6. A registrant without a phone number still gets the full WebinarGeek email journey. They just do not get WhatsApp.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The Worker reads state from the subscription data, not the event name, so a retried or dropped webhook cannot corrupt a record.
    • Post-webinar tags are cleared on re-registration so the next webinar's workflows fire again.

    Common Mistakes

    • Re-registering a person manually and creating a duplicate.

    6.3 Change the Landing Page Safely

    Owner OperationsTime 1 hourSystem GitHub, CloudflareSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    The page is live to every invite. An edit that is not previewed can break registration for hours. The page source is in a private GitHub repository, and a change is first uploaded as a preview version, so nothing reaches the public hostname until it has been checked.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes a precise change request: page, section, old text to new text, and why.
    • Prepares the plan card, and runs the landing page check after a version goes live.
    What the Operator Does
    • Apply the change in the repository, open the preview, run a test registration on it, and approve the promotion with "go".

    Every Step

    1. Fetch the latest page source first. Never edit without doing this.
    2. Edit, then save the change to the main branch with a clear note.
    3. Upload a preview version. It is not live and has its own address.
    4. Open the preview, check the change, and complete a test registration.
    5. Claude writes the plan card. Reply "go" to make the preview the live version. The landing page check runs straight after.
    6. To undo, make the previous version live again. The list of earlier versions is kept.

    Done When The change is live, the check passed, and the previous version is known.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Only public files are uploaded. Earlier deploys served documentation files and application automation source publicly.
    • Never deploy uncommitted work.

    Common Mistakes

    • Skipping the fetch and overwriting someone else's change.
    • Making a version live without a test registration.

    6.4 Set Up Website Tracking in GHL

    Owner OperationsTime 1 hourSystem GHL, Google Analytics, Tag ManagerSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Today GHL sees registrations but not page visits. The landing page is built outside GHL, and GHL's own page analytics only works on pages built inside GHL. The result is that a contact's record cannot show that they returned to the site after a webinar, which is exactly the signal that says who is ready to buy.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the setup steps and checks the result on a test contact.
    What the Operator Does
    • Add the Google Analytics integration in GHL for the external page, so visits attach to each contact.

    Every Step

    1. In GHL, open the location's tracking settings and connect the Google Analytics property used by the page.
    2. Confirm the Tag Manager container and the Stape server-side container both load on the registration page.
    3. Visit the page as a test contact and check the visit appears on that contact's record.
    4. Add the tracked pages to the list of signals used for follow-up (9.7).

    Done When A test visit shows on the contact in GHL.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Each contact's record shows form submissions and pages visited.

    Common Mistakes

    • Assuming it already works because registrations arrive.

    6.5 Build the Page to the Nine-Block Spec

    Owner Claude drafts, operations approvesTime 2 to 3 hoursSystem Landing pageSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A page that has every block but no reason for any of them converts worse than a short page where each block answers one objection and drives one action. The spec below is the reference page anatomy. Reference spec The live page is checked against it, and anything missing is a candidate change, not an assumed fault.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the live page and marks each of the nine blocks present, missing or weak.
    • Drafts the missing blocks from the offer, the buyer and the proof already in the knowledge files.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide which missing blocks are worth adding. Approve the copy before it is built.

    Every Step

    1. Open the live page on a 1366 by 768 laptop screen. The form must be visible without scrolling.
    2. Mark each of the nine blocks, in order: logo and trust strip; headline and subhead; a 60 to 90 second muted, captioned video; three proof points as numbers; the form; the named method in three to five steps; testimonials, each answering one objection; an FAQ that answers the objection list; a button that follows the reader down.
    3. Repeat the form further down the page, so no one has to hunt for it.
    4. Remove anything that answers no objection or leads off the page, such as navigation links.
    5. Check the page at phone, tablet and laptop widths, and check the date block shows the time in the visitor's own time zone with an add-to-calendar button.
    6. Ask only for what will be used: first name, last name, work email, a profile link, and a phone number only if it will be used. Every extra field costs completions.

    Done When Each block is present or consciously left out, and the form is visible on a laptop without scrolling.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Every block is there because it answers an objection or earns the action.
    • The date block is load-bearing: the time zone is right, and a calendar button and countdown are present. A wrong zone collapses show-up for reasons nobody can diagnose.

    Common Mistakes

    • Adding blocks because other pages have them.
    • A page with more than one action to take.

    6.6 Make the Thank-You Page Earn Its Keep

    Owner OperationsTime 1 hourSystem Landing page, GHLSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A thank-you page that only says thanks wastes the moment a registrant is most engaged. It has four jobs. Doing them lifts show-up, because a person who has added the event to a calendar or joined the group turns up far more often than one who did not.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Checks the live thank-you page against the four jobs and reports which are missing.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve any change to the page or the WhatsApp wording.

    Every Step

    1. Confirm the registration in plain words, with the date and time.
    2. Offer add to calendar: a Google Calendar button and a downloadable calendar file for everything else.
    3. Invite them to the community group, and offer a one-to-one WhatsApp chat for anyone who wants personal confirmation and reminders. The WhatsApp ask is what opens the 24-hour window, so it stays.
    4. Say exactly what arrives next and when: the confirmation email now, the reminders in order, the replay afterwards.

    Done When The page does all four jobs and a test registration shows each of them working.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Add to calendar is one tap on a phone.
    • The first email arrives before the registrant has left the page.

    Common Mistakes

    • A page that says only thanks.
    • Removing the WhatsApp ask because it looks like clutter.

    6.7 Avoid the Form Submit and Redirect Traps

    Owner OperationsTime 30 minSystem Landing page, WebinarGeek, GHLSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Most silent registration losses come from five small traps in how a form is captured. These are the reference rules from the playbook this one is built on. Each one is a thing to check on the live page, not a proven fault. Check against live page

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the form's behaviour on the test registration and reports whether a duplicate confirmation, a missing field or a missing contact appeared.
    What the Operator Does
    • Raise any fault with the page developer, with the test record as evidence.

    Every Step

    1. Fields before the first test. Create every custom field in the CRM before the first test submission. A value that arrives before its field exists is never mapped and never fills in later, and every message that uses it shows blank.
    2. Capture once. If the browser sends the form to GHL's own tracker as well, the submit button must not fire twice. A second capture with the join link still empty sends a second confirmation.
    3. Delay the redirect. Leaving the page the instant the form is sent can cancel the tracker's request. A short delay of about half a second protects it, most often needed on a phone on mobile data.
    4. Never suppress the confirmation email. The setting that skips the confirmation on registration means no confirmation goes out at all.
    5. Keep every key on the server. Nothing secret belongs in the page.

    Done When A test registration produces exactly one contact, one confirmation and every field filled.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Every submit is captured once.

    Common Mistakes

    • Fixing a symptom, such as a blank field, in the message instead of creating the field.

    6.8 Test the Headline and Watch the Form Abandon Number

    Owner OperationsTime 30 min per testSystem Landing page, AnalyticsSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    The conversion rate is the number everyone watches. The number nobody watches is form abandonment: visitors who started typing and stopped. They wanted to register and something in the form stopped them, usually a field that was not needed.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads page visits, form starts and registrations and reports the abandon rate, once tracking can see form starts.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide which headline pair to test and approve the change.

    Every Step

    1. Write two headlines for the same page: one benefit-led, one problem-led. Test the headline, never a second thinner page.
    2. Send equal traffic to each. Record the variant on the registration so results can be separated.
    3. Read form starts and registrations. Abandon rate is starts that did not submit.
    4. Remove one field at a time where abandonment is high. Each removal is a measurable lift.
    5. Keep the winner, and test the next idea against it.

    Done When Two headlines tested, an abandon number read, and one field removed or kept on evidence.

    What Good Looks Like

    • One change at a time.

    Common Mistakes

    • Judging a headline on a handful of visits.
    • Reading conversion alone.

    The Lessons in This Section

    • The page has nine blocks, each answering one objection, with the form above the fold.
    • The thank-you page has four jobs. Do not let it only say thanks.
    • Every invite goes to one page, so every registration is tracked the same way.
    • Walk the path once as a test registrant. A form that says success is not proof.
    • The WhatsApp ask on the thank-you page is load-bearing. Do not remove it.
    Part 7

    Nurture: Reminders and Join Links

    Two channels, each with one owner, and the four checks that keep both working.

    Master Playbook

    LeadTrafficLandingNurtureLiveAfter

    10 task cards1 sectionReviewed by Operator as runner

    The Two Channels

    STATUS: RE-READ THE WORKFLOW LIST BEFORE RELYING ON IT   AS OF: 2026-10-14

    Registration is not attendance. Show-up rate is the single link in the chain that nurture controls, and it is the one that multiplies everything after it. Two channels do the work, each with one owner.

    ChannelToolWhat it sends
    EmailWebinarGeekConfirmation on registration; reminder one day before; reminder one hour before; "We're LIVE now" at the start; follow-ups and replay after
    WhatsAppGoHighLevel (Meta-approved templates)Join link on request; four timed reminders anchored on the broadcast date

    WhatsApp through GHL uses the WhatsApp Business API. Each message must be a template approved by Meta first, so the messages are fixed and cannot be personalised by AI. SMS is not used. It is illegal as cold outreach in Germany and risky across Europe, and the exception is an opt-in where the person gave their number for that purpose. Consent basis. Guidance read on 18 October 2026 is consistent: WhatsApp marketing needs explicit, specific opt-in consent for WhatsApp itself under UK GDPR and PECR, and Meta's policy separately requires opt-in for marketing-category messages. A phone number given to register for a webinar is not marketing consent unless the form says so. So the registration form needs its own unticked WhatsApp consent box, the date, method and wording of each consent are recorded, and every message offers an easy way to stop. Whether the live form already does this is an open check (28.4), and the rule itself should be confirmed against the ICO's direct-marketing guidance and Meta's current policy before the first send.

    Two later optimisations exist but are not needed until registrations are high: AI-personalised WhatsApp through Tantra, using a connected ordinary account, and an AI voice call a few minutes before the webinar that confirms the start and the topic. Neither is tested in this account.

    7.1 Check the Confirmation and Reminder Emails

    Owner OperationsTime 30 minSystem WebinarGeekSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    WebinarGeek email edits are login only. The subject lines carry the time as text, so an event that is not at 12:00 sends people a reminder that says the wrong hour. It is the commonest small error in the cycle.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Drafts the text first from the Consolidated Document tab "WebinarGeek Emails". The person pastes it.
    What the Operator Does
    • Open the webinar, go to Emails, and for each email: open it, edit the subject and body, check the merge fields, send a preview to a team mailbox, and save.

    Every Step

    1. Sign in to WebinarGeek and open the FINTECH webinar (id 575538).
    2. Open Emails. Check the confirmation, which asks for the registrant's biggest board challenge.
    3. Check the one-day reminder, the one-hour reminder and the live-now email. Replace "12PM" where the event time differs.
    4. Send a preview of each to a team mailbox. Check the join link works.
    5. Tick the item in the new-event checklist.

    Done When Four emails checked, previewed and saved with the correct time.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Reminders carry each person's own join link.

    Common Mistakes

    • Assuming subject lines follow the broadcast time.

    7.2 Check the WhatsApp Join Link and Reminders

    Owner OperationsTime 20 minSystem GHLSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    WhatsApp reminders anchor on a custom field, webinar_broadcast_date. If it is empty or wrong on a contact, the reminders either do not fire or fire at the wrong time. Confirming it on one live contact closes the largest open question on reminder timing.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads one live contact and reports webinar_broadcast_date, watch_link_webinargeek, readable_webinar_date and readable_webinar_time.
    What the Operator Does
    • Compare the values to the broadcast. Fix the workflow, not the contact, if they differ.

    Every Step

    1. Ask: "Show the webinar fields and tags on this contact."
    2. Check the broadcast date matches the event.
    3. Check the workflow list: which are published, which are drafts.
    4. Leave the draft email workflows unpublished. Publishing one would double-send against WebinarGeek.

    Done When One live contact has the right date and the reminders anchor correctly.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The workflows that should be published are the WhatsApp reminders, the inbound join-link reply, the call reminders, the CISI applicants flow and the course-access flows. No webinar email reminder flow should be published, because WebinarGeek sends those. How many exist and which are published is current state: read it in GHL and compare with 25.5.

    Common Mistakes

    • Publishing a draft email workflow. It sends a second set of reminders.

    7.3 Specify and Build a GHL Workflow

    Owner Claude designs, operations buildsTime 1 to 2 hoursSystem GHLSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    GHL's API cannot create or edit workflows, only list them and add a contact to an existing one. So every new automation is designed in text by Claude and built by a person in the GHL interface. The spec is what makes the build correct the first time.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the spec: trigger, filters, each action and wait, the emails, tags, and exit conditions.
    • Creates what the API allows: email templates, tags and custom values, after a plan card.
    • Lists the workflow afterwards to confirm it exists and is published.
    What the Operator Does
    • Build the workflow in the GHL interface from the spec, save it as a draft, test it on one contact, and publish it after "go".

    Every Step

    1. Ask for the spec: "Write the GHL workflow spec for the follow-up to webinar no-shows." Use the template in 17.7.
    2. In GHL: Automation, Workflows, Create workflow, Start from scratch, add the trigger, add each action in order, name it FC - <purpose>, save as a draft.
    3. Use a tag as the trigger. The premium inbound webhook trigger is not used.
    4. Test on one test contact. Ask Claude to check the contact's tags and emails sent.
    5. Publish after "go". Ask Claude to list the workflow and confirm it is published.

    Done When The workflow is built, tested on one contact, published and read back.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Reminders use wait-until steps anchored on the broadcast date field.
    • Every branch has an exit: undelivered, STOP reply, and time out.

    Common Mistakes

    • Publishing before the test.
    • Tagging many contacts without checking which published workflow the tag fires. Check before adding a tag to more than a handful.

    7.4 Keep the Tags Clean

    Owner OperationsTime 10 minSystem GHLSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Tags are how the Worker, the workflows and the retargeting lists talk to each other. Older hyphenated duplicates still exist from before the Worker, and a filter built on one of them silently misses people.

    Every Step

    1. Use only the current state tags: webinar registrant, webinar attended, live webinar watched, watched webinar replay, live webinar not watched, webinar unsubscribed, clicked webinar CTA.
    2. Ignore the older hyphenated duplicates in new filters.
    3. Remember a webinar<n> tag is created automatically for each new broadcast by the daily dashboard run. Verify it the next day.

    Done When Every filter and workflow uses the current names.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Tag writes are additive. The chat never removes a tag.

    Common Mistakes

    • Filtering on watched equals false for no-shows (9.2 explains why).

    7.5 Read the Attendance Sync Correctly

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 10 min per webinarSystem WebinarGeek, GHLSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Attendance data arrives late and can be wrong in two ways. If the follow-up starts at the end time, it reads nothing and tells every attendee they were missed. If the sync fails for a person, they carry no tag, and no tag looks the same as did not watch. Both cost real sales, so the rules are fixed in advance.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • After the session, reads the viewer list from WebinarGeek and the tags in GHL, and reports anyone whose tag and viewing time disagree.
    What the Operator Does
    • Wait before trusting a no-show list. Read any alert Claude raises.

    Every Step

    1. Do not read attendance at the end of the session. Viewer events arrive one to two hours later, which is normal.
    2. Start the attended and no-show branches from the completed tag, or wait at least two hours after the scheduled end.
    3. Count a person as attended by their watch duration, in seconds. Under 30 seconds of viewing does not count.
    4. Never filter on the watched flag alone. Filtering on the wrong flag has sent "sorry you missed it" to people who watched the whole session.
    5. If a registrant has no attendance tag at all, the sync failed for them. Treat them as a no-show for follow-up and raise an alert, so the gap is checked at the source.
    6. Compare the tagged attendees against the viewer list in WebinarGeek statistics before the follow-up goes.

    Done When Every registrant has an attendance tag, and any person without one has been alerted and treated as a no-show.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The no-show list is built from WebinarGeek, never from a GHL tag on its own.

    Common Mistakes

    • Starting the follow-up at the session end time.
    • Reading no tag as did not attend without raising an alert.

    7.6 Put the Four Guards on Every Reminder

    Owner OperationsTime 30 minSystem GHL, WebinarGeekSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A reminder that fires with no join link, or fires late in a burst, damages trust and show-up. Four guards prevent it. They are built into every wait and send step, and tested without waiting days.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the guard rules into every workflow spec and reads back a test contact to confirm each fired.
    What the Operator Does
    • Build the guards in GHL from the spec. Run the 65-minute test before a webinar goes out.

    Every Step

    1. Anchor every wait on the broadcast date field, as wait until the date minus the offset. Never use a plain wait of a number of days.
    2. Check the join link field is not empty before every send.
    3. If the time for a reminder has already passed for that person, skip the step.
    4. Add an exit on a STOP reply or unsubscribe.
    5. Test without waiting days: move one test contact's broadcast date to 65 minutes from now and watch the short reminders fire. Never edit the workflow's offsets to test.
    6. If the date changes, follow the date-change checklist below, in order.

    Done When A test contact received every short reminder on time, with a working link, and a late registrant received none of the old ones.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The sub-account time zone matches the webinar's time zone.

    Common Mistakes

    • Plain waits of a number of days.
    • Editing offsets to test.
    • Changing the broadcast date and assuming reminders follow.

    7.7 Write Reminders to the Copy Rules

    Owner Claude drafts, operations approvesTime 1 hourSystem WebinarGeek, GHLSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    People skim in inverse proportion to urgency. A long message at the last minute is not read. The rules below are the reference copy rules. Reference rules Check each live message against them before the next event.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Drafts every reminder to the word counts and checks the number of links and the wording.
    What the Operator Does
    • Read, edit and approve each message. Paste email text into the webinar tool by hand.

    Every Step

    1. Write the day-before email at 180 to 220 words: what to prepare before joining.
    2. Write the one-hour email at 80 to 100 words: the join link again.
    3. Write the we-are-live message at 50 to 70 words, with one link.
    4. Put exactly one link in every message. Two links is a decision, and a decision at the last minute is a lost attendee.
    5. Write every WhatsApp reminder as a plain statement of fact: the session starts tomorrow at 12:00, here is your link. Urgency words can turn a utility message into a marketing one, which is charged at a higher rate and needs documented opt-in.
    6. Send the day-before reminder at 8am in the recipient's own time zone, not 8am in the sender's. Save each registrant's time zone on the contact. In GHL, set the workflow to the contact's time zone and resume waits from 8:00. A contact with none falls back to the account time zone.
    7. Run every draft through a spam checker before it goes near a real list.

    Done When Every message is within its word range, has one link, and the day-before reminder lands at 8am recipient time.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The WhatsApp wording is a flat fact, not a nudge.

    Common Mistakes

    • Two links in one reminder.
    • Urgency words in a WhatsApp template.
    • A fixed UK time for everyone.

    7.8 Measure Show-Up Against Reference Bands

    Owner OperationsTime 15 min per webinarSystem Dashboard, WebinarGeekSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Roughly half of the people who register never turn up, because life happened and nothing reminded them hard enough. Nurture is the cheapest lift in the whole funnel, since these people are already paid for. But a target taken from someone else's funnel is a guess. The bands are for orientation. The number that counts is FINTECH's own show-up rate.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads registrants and attendees from WebinarGeek, computes the show-up rate, and says which webinars it is compared with.
    What the Operator Does
    • Compare the rate with the last three webinars first, and with the bands second.

    Every Step

    1. Compute show-up as attendees divided by registrants. Read both from WebinarGeek.
    2. Compare it with the last three webinars at the same distance from the event.
    3. Compare it with the reference bands, and say plainly that they are not results.
    4. Record what changed in nurture since the last event, so a rise or fall can be explained.

    Done When A show-up rate with its comparison webinars and one named lever to change.

    Labelled, Not Measured

    The three bars above come from the reference playbook. They are shown so a reader knows the shape of the target. They are not FINTECH results. Replace them with the dashboard's own numbers as soon as they exist.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The comparison is with FINTECH's own history.

    Common Mistakes

    • Quoting a reference band as a result.

    7.9 Know the Extra Reminder Channels

    Owner OperationsTime 15 minSystem GHL, TantraSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    Email and WhatsApp carry the reminders today. Two more channels exist and are left unused. They are listed so that a decision to add one is made on facts, with the right consent in place.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the plan card for any new channel, including what consent it needs and what it costs.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide whether a new channel is worth adding. It needs a tested opt-in on the form first.

    Every Step

    1. Read the table below and the badge on each channel.
    2. SMS Available goes only in the last hour, one link each, and only to people who opted in to texts on the form.
    3. AI voice call Potential is a call of under 30 seconds at go-live that says who is calling, that it is an automated call, that the session is starting now and that the link is in their WhatsApp and email. It stops calling anyone who says no.
    4. Add the matching opt-in boxes to the form before any message goes. A box left unticked means no tag and no message on that channel.
    5. Test on one contact before any wider use.

    Done When A decision on each channel, with the consent step named.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The opt-in is recorded with the date and wording.

    Common Mistakes

    • Calling or texting people who only gave a number to register.

    7.10 See the Whole Reminder and Follow-Up Flow

    Owner OperationsTime 15 minSystem Tantra, GHL, WebinarGeekSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    The reminder flow is the show-up engine. The follow-up flow splits by what each person did. Seeing both on one line shows where FINTECH's current set-up has gaps. It is the reference model. Reference model Nobody leaves the funnel. People only change speed.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Marks which touches already exist in WebinarGeek and GHL, and which are gaps.
    What the Operator Does
    • Choose which gaps to close first.

    Every Step

    1. Read the line from left to right. The first six points are the reminders before the session.
    2. Check which of them exist today, and the wording of each.
    3. Read the attended branch: four touches over three days, with a real deadline.
    4. Read the no-show branch: the replay at one day, the one thing missed at two days, the closing replay at five days.
    5. Check that everyone still on the list enters the 52-week engine.

    Done When A list of touches that exist and touches that do not, with the first gap named.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The no-show branch is warm: these people registered.

    Common Mistakes

    • Treating the no-show branch as a lost cause.
    • A replay link with no expiry.

    The Lessons in This Section

    • Never read attendance at the end of a session. It arrives one to two hours late.
    • A registrant with no attendance tag is a no-show and an alert.
    • Email is WebinarGeek's. WhatsApp is GHL's. The Worker is the only bridge.
    • Subject lines hold the time as text. Check them every event.
    • GHL workflows are designed by Claude and built by a person. A draft stays a draft until it is tested.
