    Part 11

    Infrastructure and Deliverability

    Domains, mailboxes, DNS, limits and the health report, with the rule that every change is checked first and made once.

    Master Playbook

    8 task cards1 sectionReviewed by Operator as runner, Technical owner

    The Rule and the Estate

    STATUS: CURRENT   AS OF: 2026-10-19

    Infrastructure is where a small mistake damages every later send. A broken DNS record, a duplicated SPF record, or cold email sent from the main brand domain can cost weeks of deliverability. DNS is the public address book of a domain: it tells the world which servers may send its mail. This part exists so every change is checked first, and made once.

    The Rule for Every Infrastructure Change

    Never change or delete an existing record. Add new records only, under a new subdomain, beside what exists. Before any change Claude does a read-only check of the name: who hosts its DNS, whether the team's Cloudflare account holds the zone, every record already at or under the name, and the main domain's mail records, which must not move. Claude then shows a plan card and waits for 'go'. Cold email never sends from the main brand domain or its subdomains. Transactional and marketing email never share a subdomain.

    Which Account Holds the DNS

    DomainsDNS lives inWho can change it
    The registration page and dashboard hostnames, and the five calendar sender domainsCloudflare, the team's own accountThat account's login
    The eleven Instantly cold-email domainsA second Cloudflare accountThat owner's console only
    The main brand website and its Google Workspace emailA different Cloudflare accountThat account's owner. Ask which one holds it.

    The Sending Estate

    • Calendar (Tantra): 20 warmed Google Workspace mailboxes across five root domains plus subdomains, about 250 invites per mailbox per day. Their calendars record Yes, Maybe and No.
    • Cold email (Instantly): eleven domains and fifty mailboxes. Three are on fintech-named domains and eight on .co domains that send through a third-party provider.
    • The 20 mailboxes live in a separate Google Workspace. Automation cannot act as the team's own address, which is why shared files are owned by the operations account and shared to the team.

    11.1 Add or Check DNS Records

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 20 minSystem CloudflareSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Mail authentication fails silently. Two SPF records break authentication with no error. A mail-tracking record set to proxied instead of DNS only stops the tool working. The steps below prevent those.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Does the read-only check, shows what already exists, and prepares the plan card for any new record in the team's Cloudflare account.
    What the Operator Does
    • Add the record exactly as the requesting tool shows, in the DNS host's own screen. This is always a person's click for domains Claude cannot reach.

    Every Step

    1. Open the Cloudflare dashboard, pick the domain, then DNS, Records, Add record.
    2. Enter the type, name and value exactly as the tool shows. Some DNS hosts add the root domain automatically: enter members, not members.example.com.
    3. Mail tracking and DKIM records are DNS only (grey cloud), never proxied.
    4. Exactly one SPF record per name.
    5. Check with Google Admin Toolbox, MXToolbox Domain Health or dnschecker. Pass means SPF valid, DKIM valid, DMARC present, MX correct, no duplicates.

    Done When Every record shows valid and the checks pass.

    What Good Looks Like

    • New things go beside existing ones, never on top.

    Common Mistakes

    • Overwriting an existing record because the name looked unused.

    11.2 Add a New Sending Domain in GHL

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 1 hour plus DNS timeSystem GHL, CloudflareSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    GHL restricted sending from the account, so client email (onboarding, programme updates) needs a dedicated subdomain, for example members. on the brand domain. It keeps client email apart from the main mailboxes and from all marketing and cold outreach.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Does the read-only check first: who holds the DNS, whether the subdomain exists, whether the domain is already added in GHL, and the root records that must not change.
    What the Operator Does
    • Use one browser profile, not incognito, with GHL in one tab and the DNS host in another.

    Every Step

    1. In GHL: Settings, Email Services, Dedicated Domain and IP, Add Domain. Enter the subdomain and Add and Verify.
    2. If GHL shows Connect or Authorize, approve it in the pop-up and GHL adds every record itself.
    3. Otherwise add the records by hand: SPF (TXT), DKIM (TXT), two MX records, a click-tracking CNAME (DNS only), and a DMARC record v=DMARC1; p=none;.
    4. Click Verify in GHL. Every record must turn green. DNS can take minutes to 48 hours.
    5. Send a test email to an external inbox and check the headers show SPF and DKIM pass.

    Done When All records green and a test email passes SPF and DKIM.

    What Good Looks Like

    • A dedicated subdomain keeps transactional and marketing apart.

    Common Mistakes

    • Setting the click-tracking CNAME to proxied.

    11.3 Add a Calendar Sender Mailbox

    Owner OperationsTime 30 min plus 2 to 3 weeks warm-upSystem Google Workspace, TantraSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Calendar capacity is bounded by the mailboxes and by the shared Google quota. More mailboxes are more capacity, but only after warm-up. A mailbox that joins a live campaign cold damages the domain.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the brief for the person: the user to create, the domain records, the permission to grant and the Tantra settings.
    • Reads the senders afterwards through the connector and confirms the count, the warm status and the daily limit.
    What the Operator Does
    • Create the user in the Workspace. For a new domain add MX, SPF, DKIM and a DMARC record with a reporting address. In the Workspace admin screen, let the calendar service account act for the mailbox (see below). In Tantra, Accounts, paste the address, set Guests per Day and the warm status, and save.

    Every Step

    1. Create the Workspace user.
    2. For a new domain, add the Google MX, SPF v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all, DKIM, and DMARC p=none with reporting.
    3. Operations lets the calendar service account act for the mailbox (domain-wide delegation, explained below).
    4. Add the address in Tantra under Verify and Add Accounts. It must show Connected. If it shows Disconnected, wait a few minutes and use Re-authenticate All.
    5. Set Guests per Day: about 20 while the mailbox is cold and about 50 once it has warmed (reference starting points; FINTECH's own setting is in 11.7). Set Warm to Cold or Warmed to match. Never leave the default in place.
    6. Warm it up for 2 to 3 weeks before it joins a live campaign.

    Done When The mailbox is connected, limited and warming.

    Permission (scope)In plain words
    Calendar and Calendar eventsCreate the invite in the mailbox's own calendar and read the reply (Yes, Maybe, No).
    Gmail sendSend mail as the mailbox.
    User email and profileKnow which mailbox it is acting for.
    Gmail modify (cold email only)Tell a real reply from an auto-responder. Without it a sender shows as Calendar only.
    Gmail read only (only for a reply reader, 11.8)Read bounces and replies so they can be recorded. Not granted when last recorded (undated, UNVERIFIED now).

    The reference method grants these as a set, once per Workspace: one service account with delegation covers every mailbox in the same Workspace. FINTECH's calendar account is recorded as Calendar only, acting for the 20 sender mailboxes. Check the live grant before assuming more.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Warm-up is not shortcut.
    • The Tantra sender list, read through the connector, shows the expected count and limits.

    Common Mistakes

    • Adding a mailbox the week of a webinar.
    • Leaving the default daily limit in place.

    11.4 Add a Cold-Email Domain and Mailboxes

    Owner OperationsTime 1 hour plus warm-upSystem Instantly, supplier, second Cloudflare accountSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Cold-email domains wear out. They are bought and set up through the inbox supplier or Namecheap and live in the second Cloudflare account. A new domain is a replacement, not an addition, for one whose bounce rate has risen.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the mailbox list and campaign limits through the connector once the supplier has finished, and reports anything not connected.

    Every Step

    1. Buy the domain and mailboxes through the supplier or the registrar.
    2. After setup, check every mailbox is Connected, warm-up is on and the daily limit is set.
    3. Check the tracking domain is active: in Instantly, Settings, Tracking domain, with the CNAME in Cloudflare.
    4. Rotate any credential shared with the vendor once they finish.
    5. Add the new domain to the monitored list so the weekly health check covers it.

    Done When The domain is connected, limited and in the monitor.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Every domain that sends is in the monitor. The cold-email domains were missing from it until September.

    Common Mistakes

    • Leaving a vendor credential unchanged after the setup.

    11.5 Raise DMARC Enforcement

    Owner OperationsTime Review 1 hourSystem CloudflareSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    DMARC is the policy that tells receiving mail servers what to do with mail that claims to be from the domain but fails the checks. The five calendar root domains publish a policy of none with reports to a monitored address, which only watches. Enforcement protects the brand from spoofing, but raising it too early would block legitimate mail from a sender that is not aligned.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the aggregate reports and recommends. It does not change DNS.
    What the Operator Does
    • Operations changes the policy, after a preview, and only after reports show every sender aligned.

    Every Step

    1. Collect one to two weeks of DMARC aggregate reports.
    2. Check every legitimate sender is aligned. SPF also authorises four third-party senders (SendGrid, Resend, SparkPost and Cloudflare Email).
    3. Preview the change to quarantine and read what it would do.
    4. Apply it only after reading the preview.
    5. Read the next reports before moving toward reject.

    Done When The policy is raised and the next reports show no legitimate mail failing.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The eight .co domains are already at reject but have no reporting address, so their results cannot be seen. Fixing that needs the owner's console.

    Common Mistakes

    • Raising enforcement before reading the reports.

    11.6 Read the Deliverability Report

    Owner OperationsTime 15 min per weekSystem Monitoring, dashboardSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    A weekly check looks at every domain that sends mail. A health figure that scored web hosts and tracking records as if they sent email described web hosting, not deliverability. The report now scores only domains that hold a live mailbox.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the latest report and the dashboard panel, and names which domains need action.

    Every Step

    1. Read the weekly report on the dashboard.
    2. Read bounce rates, not counts, per campaign (the bars in 16.16 show why).
    3. A domain that sends through a third-party mail service can show a warning for the missing Google SPF record. That is expected. Label it so it does not read as a fault.
    4. Act on a rising bounce rate before the next wave.

    Done When The team knows which domains are healthy and which need action.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Scored scope: the thirty domains that hold a live mailbox. At the last count, 22 were good, 8 warned and none were bad.

    Common Mistakes

    • Reading a total over all domains. It averages in domains that never send.

    11.7 Limits and Capacity: A Worked Example

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 20 minSystem Tantra, InstantlySafety Read

    Why It Matters

    How many people can be reached in a day is set by the mailboxes, their warm-up and a shared quota, not by the size of the list. Two sets of numbers are quoted in this playbook. They are both starting points, and they answer different questions. This card shows the sum and which limit binds.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Does the sum for the next wave: audience, working days to the event, mailboxes, the limit that binds. Shows it on the plan card.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide how many days to spread a large send over, or whether to add mailboxes.

    Every Step

    1. Reference starting points for a new account (teaching model): 20 a day per mailbox while it warms, about 50 once warmed, never above 200 a day for calendar invites, bounce under 1 percent, reject any bought list with more than 2 percent duplicates.
    2. FINTECH's own estate (from its own history): about 250 invites per warmed mailbox per day, so 20 mailboxes is 5,000 a day on paper. One Google service account delivers roughly 1,500 invites a day, because mailboxes that share it share one quota.
    3. Reconcile them. The reference 200 cap is a cautious ceiling for a young account. The 250 per mailbox is what this warmed estate has been set to. Neither is a law. The lower limit that applies is the one that binds, and for FINTECH that is the shared service-account quota, not the mailbox figure.
    4. Worked example, reference model: two domains with three mailboxes each is 6 mailboxes. Warming: 6 x 20 = 120 a day. Warmed: 6 x 50 = 300 a day. A 5-day send at 300 a day reaches 1,500 people.
    5. Worked example, FINTECH: an audience of 6,000 over 5 working days needs 1,200 a day. That is inside the 1,500 service-account ceiling and well inside 5,000 on paper, so it fits. 6,000 over 2 days needs 3,000 a day and does not.
    6. If it does not fit, the answer is more days, more mailboxes, or another service account. Never a higher cap on one account.

    Done When The day's volume is below the binding limit, and the plan card shows the sum.

    LimitStarting pointWhat breaks if ignored
    Mailbox while warmingAbout 20 a dayA cold mailbox burns the domain, slowly and visibly late
    Mailbox once warmedAbout 50 a day (reference), about 250 (this estate)Spam filtering and bounces rise
    Bounce rateUnder 1 percent on a list, stop an inbox at 5 percentReputation falls fastest through bounces
    Duplicates in a bought listReject above 2 percentThe same person is contacted twice
    Service-account quotaAbout 1,500 invites a dayInvites silently stay Not Sent and response dies

    What Good Looks Like

    • The plan card shows audience, days, volume a day and the binding limit side by side.

    Common Mistakes

    • Reading mailboxes times the per-mailbox cap as the real capacity.
    • Quoting the reference numbers as FINTECH results.

    11.8 Calendar-Invite Copy Rules and the Reply Reader

    Owner Operations, ClaudeTime 30 minSystem Tantra, Google CalendarSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A calendar invite lands in the recipient's own calendar, so its title and first lines are all that is read. The rules below come from the reference method and are checked against the approved FINTECH titles in Part 4. The reply handling is marked Potential today: a reply that says stop or unsubscribe is being wired to move the person onto Tantra's unsubscribe list automatically.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Drafts the invite to the rules and checks the live campaign against the approved text before anything goes out.
    • Would run the reply reader once built: it reads the sender mailboxes about every 60 seconds and records each reply.
    What the Operator Does
    • Approve the copy. Check that a reply of stop or unsubscribe reaches Tantra's unsubscribe list once the automation is live.

    Every Step

    1. Title like a meeting, not an ad. Plain words, the topic and the outcome. No dollar sign, no percent sign, and not the word 'free'.
    2. Promise in the first two lines. Who it is for and what they leave with. The join link sits lower down.
    3. One line that makes declining easy, so fewer people report the invite.
    4. Every link carries a source tag so registrations can be traced.
    5. Same text for every guest. No merge fields, so there is nothing to render wrongly.
    6. Keep the approved text and compare the live campaign to it.
    7. The reply reader (not built): reads accepted as Yes, tentative as Maybe, declined as No, records it on the contact, and puts every bounce on a do-not-contact tab. Bounces and opt-outs also go on Tantra's unsubscribe list.

    Done When The live campaign matches the approved text, and the status of the reply reader is decided and recorded.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The first two lines carry the promise before the calendar preview cuts them off.

    Common Mistakes

    • A long description that buries the promise.
    • A date or time that differs from the event platform's.

    The Lessons in This Section

    • Add beside, never overwrite. Check every name first.
    • Warm-up is not optional. A cold mailbox harms the domain.
    • The lowest limit binds. Do the sum before the send.
    • Score deliverability on the domains that send, in rates.
    Part 15

    How the Tools Are Wired

    For every tool: what it is, how Claude reaches it, what it can read and write, and what needs a person's approval. Then registration, the Worker, every workflow, WhatsApp, the connector, the change rules and the risks.

    Master Playbook

    10 task cards14 sectionsReviewed by Operator as runner, Technical owner

    What This Part Is

    In One Minute

    People register on the landing page. WebinarGeek hosts the event and sends every email. A small Cloudflare program, the Worker, is the only thing that copies state between WebinarGeek and the CRM. The CRM, GoHighLevel, keeps the record of each person and sends every WhatsApp message. Instantly and Tantra bring people to the page. A sheet logs registrations. Claude reaches each of these through its connector, reads freely, and writes only after the operator types "go" or "send now".

    STATUS: CURRENT UNLESS A TABLE SAYS OTHERWISE; LIVE STATE DRIFTS, RE-READ IT   AS OF: 2026-10-19

    Parts 1 to 14 explain what the funnel does and how to run it. This part explains how the tools are wired: which tool owns which step, what happens when someone registers, what each automation does, what the tags and fields mean, and the rules for changing any of it. For every tool it says what it is, how Claude reaches it (a connector tool, the tool's API, or a person in the tool's own screen), what Claude can read, what it can write, and what needs a person's approval.

    It is the part to read when something behaves unexpectedly, when a new person takes over, or before changing anything that is live. Anything that reads a live state, such as which workflows are published or which Instantly campaigns are active, is a dated snapshot. Re-read it before quoting it.

    The Tools, One Job Each, and How Claude Reaches Each

    The rule that keeps it untangled: WebinarGeek owns email, GHL owns WhatsApp, and the Cloudflare Worker is the only thing that writes between them.

    Two channels never cross. WebinarGeek email runs straight from the registration and bypasses the Worker entirely. GHL WhatsApp runs from the tags the Worker writes. Secrets are never saved in the shared files: the GHL token, the WebinarGeek signing string and the Summit form secret are stored as secrets in Cloudflare, and the local development file is ignored.

    Registration Capture in Detail

    One submit fans out to four destinations. They are independent: a failure in one does not block the registration, except the first.

    #DestinationWhat it isIf it fails
    1WebinarGeek, through the registration backendA registration request for the FINTECH clientThe registration genuinely fails. The only blocking one.
    2Google SheetsA post to the sheet's automation, the reply is not readLogged and swallowed
    3GoHighLevelAn embedded GHL form and tracking code, submitted as a real form submitSilent
    4The thank-you pageA handoff to the next page, redirect after 600 millisecondsThe page loads without the personalised detail

    How the GHL Write Really Happens

    This is the part most often misread. The webhook address in the page is deliberately empty: it is an inert fallback. The real write goes through GHL's form-tracking code. The page carries a hidden GHL form whose fields sit off-screen, not marked as hidden, because the tracker ignores genuinely hidden fields. Four fields are computed in the browser before the submit.

    FieldFormatBuilt by
    readable_webinar_dateA human-readable date, Europe/LondonThe page
    readable_webinar_timeA human-readable time, Europe/LondonThe page
    webinar_broadcast_dateYYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss. The machine field every reminder wait anchors on.The page
    watch_link_webinargeekThe registrant's own join linkThe reply from destination 1
    • The submit is a real form submit, so the browser validates and the tracker sees it.
    • The 600 millisecond redirect delay is deliberate. It lets the parallel posts leave the browser.
    • Timezone must match in two places. The page writes Europe/London and the Worker's webinar timezone setting must also be Europe/London. If one moves, direct WebinarGeek registrants and landing-page registrants get disagreeing times. Nothing enforces this.

    The Worker in Detail

    WebinarGeek sends a message (a webhook) on registration, viewer and unsubscribe events. The Worker verifies the signature, finds or creates the GHL contact on email, fills the webinar fields, and sets state tags. A Worker is a small program that runs in Cloudflare's cloud.

    Design decision: the Worker reads state from the subscription data, not from the event name. Any event brings GHL fully up to date, and a retried message gives the same result. A dropped or duplicated message cannot corrupt a record.

    Events subscribed in WebinarGeek: new registration, unsubscribed, new viewer, new live viewer, new replay viewer, no show. WebinarGeek does not generate a signing secret, so a long random string is typed into its webhook settings and stored as the same value in the Worker.

    TagAdded whenRemoved when
    webinar registrantAny event for an active registrantThey unsubscribe
    webinar attendedThey watched in any form, live or replayThey register for a new webinar
    live webinar watchedThey watched the live broadcastThey register for a new webinar
    watched webinar replayThey watched the replayThey register for a new webinar
    live webinar not watchedThe broadcast ended and they did not watch liveThey register for a new webinar
    webinar unsubscribedThey unsubscribeThey register for a new webinar
    clicked webinar CTAThey click a call to action during the webinarThey register for a new webinar

    Why tags are cleared on re-registration. GHL fires 'tag added' only if the tag was not already present. Clearing the post-webinar tags on a new registration lets the next webinar add them again and re-fire the workflows. Without it, a repeat attendee silently stops triggering anything.

    Safety Behaviours

    • A missing field is skipped, not fatal, with a logged warning.
    • A phone number is sent only when it is valid international format. GHL rejects the whole update on a bad number. The number the landing page captured is never overwritten or blanked.
    • Response codes: 200 synced or safely ignored, 401 bad signature, 502 GHL rejected it, with GHL's error text in the log. Every run logs the event, the email, the contact id and the tags.
    • Two more automations live in the same Worker: the Summit site forms, and every form on the main website.

    Every GHL Workflow

    STATUS: STANDING DESCRIPTION; WHICH WORKFLOWS ARE PUBLISHED IS CURRENT STATE, SEE 25.5   AS OF: 2026-10-20

    What each workflow is for. Whether it is published, and how many exist, changes without notice: it is kept in 25.5 GHL Workflows: What Is Published and must be re-read in GHL before it is quoted.

    The Workflows That Run the Funnel

    WorkflowWhat it does
    Fintech whatsapp reminder workflowThe WhatsApp reminder sequence. Waits anchored on webinar_broadcast_date. Four template reminders.
    Reply to Inbound WhatsApp MessagesFires on a customer reply, matches 'send me my join link', waits 0.2 minutes, sends the join link by WhatsApp.
    Call remindersReminds a booked caller before a sales call (9.16).
    CISI applicantsThe CISI-branded application flow, separate from the main one.
    Grant Course AccessGives a paid contact course access.
    Course grant access, LecturersThe same, for the lecturer cohort.

    What Must Never Be Published

    WebinarGeek sends every webinar email: confirmation, reminders, follow-up and replay. A GHL workflow that also sends webinar email would double-send. So GHL workflows named for webinar email reminders and follow-up stay unpublished, and are deleted or renamed with a zz- prefix so none is switched on by accident. GHL's stock starter workflows are the same hazard.

    GHL's API is read-only for workflows: it returns names and status, never triggers or steps. Workflows are built in GHL's own screen by the team, from a spec Claude writes (17.7).

    WhatsApp Automation in Detail

    The design trick. The thank-you page asks the registrant to WhatsApp the words 'send me my join link'. That inbound message opens WhatsApp's 24-hour customer-service window. That is why the confirmation can be a free-form message instead of a paid template, and why the reminders that follow land reliably. The ask on the thank-you page is load-bearing.

    Workflow 1: Reply to Inbound WhatsApp Messages

    • Rough edge: a contact who fails the guard exits silently, with no notification and no fallback. The undelivered, STOP and time-out branches are empty.

    Workflow 2: The Reminder Workflow

    • Trigger: a tracking event from the registration form on the landing page. First check: the contact has a phone number.
    • Waits are wait-until steps anchored on webinar_broadcast_date. Four reminders, each an approved WhatsApp template.
    • The morning reminder is 4 hours 30 minutes before the broadcast (06:30 for an 11:00 webinar). It was 6 hours (05:00) and was changed deliberately.
    • Structural risk: offsets are relative, so an unusually early or late broadcast shifts every reminder, including into unsociable hours. Look at it whenever the schedule changes.

    WhatsApp follow-up is not implemented. After the webinar, follow-up is WebinarGeek email only. To add WhatsApp follow-up: a wait step at the end of the reminder workflow, then follow-up templates over the next two to three days. Potential

    Three application forms exist. Two have their own sheet, automation and Calendly, kept separate so the partner funnel never touches the main pipeline.

    FINTECHThe main application pageProgramme ApplicantsThe 15-minute booking event
    CISIThe CISI-branded pageCISI ApplicantsA separate CISI event
    Future cohortThe future-cohort pageProgramme Applicants (shares the main automation)The 15-minute booking event
    • Duplicate-send guard: any non-empty column R counts as handled. That stopped rows the older workflow had already emailed being emailed twice. A value starting FAILED still retries. Leave it on.
    • Sender: the name FINTECH Circle, from the boards address, failure alerts to the applications address. The from address must be a verified Send mail as alias on the account that installed the automation, or every send throws an error. A built-in check tells which case it is.
    • Signature banner: an inline image, not a hotlinked one, because hotlinked images are blocked by default and show as a broken box.
    • Never re-run Setup Spreadsheet on a live sheet. It rewrites the column layout.
    • Saving is not deploying. The automation picks up changes only on a new deployment, so saved copies drift from what is live.

    All custom fields are text. Other tags that drive automation besides the seven state tags: cisi_applicant (the CISI form to the CISI workflow), Summit_Attendee and Summit_ContactUs (the Worker's Summit routing), and lecturers (set by hand, to the lecturers course-access workflow).

    Legacy Duplicate Tags: Never Use in a New Filter

    A workflow filtered on a legacy name silently matches the earlier cohorts and misses the current one. Which legacy tags exist at any time is read from the GHL tag list (see 25.2). GHL email templates come in families: sales call emails, webinar emails, remarketing, cohort and bulletin emails, and course templates. The rule: when a template exists twice under different ids, check the id before editing, because the unused copy is the easy one to edit by mistake. The inventory of templates as last recorded is in 25.2.

    The Connector: What It Enforces

    The connector is a Cloudflare Worker with sign-in and a passphrase held by the operations team. Its safety rules are built into the tools, so the chat cannot get them wrong. For the Tantra, Instantly, GHL and WebinarGeek systems, use these tools and not the vendors' own connectors.

    What the Wave Tools Enforce

    • The broadcast must be upcoming and dated the same day as the event. Ended or cancelled broadcasts are refused.
    • Invite copy comes from the canonical V1 to V5 campaigns. Its calendar line is rewritten for this event, and any other date or time left in the copy blocks the wave. That is what once sent about 4,000 invites with a July date (historical incident).
    • Leads: unused only; never anyone marked on any tab, contacted in Tantra or emailed by Instantly (unless the operator explicitly asks to recontact); minus RSVP and attendee exclusions, the suppression list and blocked domains; minus excluded geographies and title words.
    • Every campaign: balanced distribution, Europe/London, the WebinarGeek broadcast linked, RSVPs auto-registered, the variationN tag.
    • Wave names continue after any wave already created that day.
    • The exclusion data is published by the daily dashboard run. If it is more than 72 hours old, the preview refuses. The fix is a successful daily run, not a workaround.

    Bulk Jobs

    Tools marked 'repeat with a job id' process a batch per call and return how many remain. Keep calling with the same job id until none remain, and report the tally. A job is never applied twice and survives a dropped chat for seven days. Batch sizes: 1,000 leads per call to Instantly, 20 contacts per call for GHL tags and workflow enrolment, 40 per call for suppression and WebinarGeek registration.

    The New-Webinar Email Flow in Tools

    List campaigns, read the latest in full, show a plan card with the replacements, then on 'go' duplicate it, preview the leads, plan card, 'go', add the leads, preview the copy with the operator, and on 'send now' activate. Activation checks the mailboxes, the schedule end date and that the campaign has leads.

    The Landing Page Repository

    Source: a private GitHub repository on the main branch. Plain pages: the registration page, thank-you, application, future-cohort application, CISI application, application-processing, payment-success, questionnaire thank-you and the webinar replay page, plus a phone-field helper and images.

    Hosting: a Cloudflare Worker serving the registration hostname and the two pro-domain hostnames, assets only. The GrowthClub developer also deploys from this repository. Registrations post to the sheet's automation and the Work Tracker, to the registration backend, and to GHL through external form tracking.

    Who edits: the operations workspace, using Claude Code. The chat cannot make or deploy changes. From the chat, write the change request precisely: page, section, old text to new text, why. Deploys never add, move or remove a hostname. Only public files are uploaded: until 28 September, internal documents and automation sources were publicly readable.

    The Change Levels, Plan Card and Change Log

    LevelExamplesRule
    0 ReadAny lookup, analysis, dashboard fetchFree
    1 DraftDocs, Canva designs, an Instantly draft campaign, a GHL email template, an inactive scenario, a Worker on a preview routeAllowed with the tool's approval. Say it is a draft and where it is.
    2 Live, reversibleGHL tags on a few contacts, a new DNS record, promoting a landing-page variant, activating an automationState the plan, the scope (how many records) and the rollback. Wait for 'go', then do it and log it.
    3 Reaches people, irreversibleActivating Instantly, sending email, registering people in bulk, bulk tag writes, any Tantra calendar campaignShow the exact preview (audience, count, copy, time). Proceed only on 'send now' for that preview. Tantra sends only through the wave tools.
    Never from chatEditing or deleting existing DNS records, DMARC policy, deleting campaigns, contacts or data, payments and refunds, GDPR erasure, changing sharing on core files, anything on another client's systemsA brief to the operations team

    Always, for level 1 and above: re-read the live state first, check suppression and exclusions for anything that reaches people, re-read afterwards to confirm it took effect (vendor counters are not proof), and log it in the change log, a Google Doc named 'FINTECH Funnel, Change Log'. One entry per change: date and time (UK), who asked, level, system, what changed, variant id, how to undo, result.

    How Instantly and the Outreach Sheet Are Organised

    One Instantly campaign per webinar, named 'Webinar <n> - <date>'. Ids change every webinar, so Claude always lists and never relies on a stored id. The current pattern is three concurrent campaigns per webinar: two cold variants A/B-testing a Personal angle against a Value angle, and one retarget campaign aimed at the previous webinar's yes and maybe no-shows. Earlier campaigns are completed or bounce-protected.

    The Master Outreach Sheet has one tab per webinar and a lead is marked once invited, so nobody is emailed for two webinars running. A shared suppression list sits across campaigns (unsubscribed, bounced, off-persona). It is not synced with the GHL unsubscribed tag.

    15.1 Add a New Automation the Safe Way

    Owner Claude designs, operations buildsTime Half a daySystem GHL, Worker, MakeSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    The default home for a new automation is GHL, because workflows are moving there. Anything that writes GHL tags can fire a published workflow that sends WhatsApp or email. An automation that is switched on before it has been tested on one record is how a mass send happens by accident.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the spec: trigger, filters, each action and wait, the templates, tags, exit conditions and the switch-off rule.
    • Lists which published workflows the tags it writes would trigger.
    What the Operator Does
    • Build it inactive in GHL's own screen. Run it on one test record. Show the result. Then ask to activate.

    Every Step

    1. Design the spec (7.3 and the template in 17.7).
    2. Build the automation inactive in GHL from the spec. Use Make only for cross-tool glue.
    3. Run it on one test record, then on two contacts as in 15.9. Read the contact's tags and any messages sent.
    4. Plan card, then 'go' to activate.
    5. Record the trigger, the action, the owner and how to switch it off in the change log.

    Done When The automation is active, tested on one record, and recorded with how to switch it off.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Every automation that writes tags lists the workflows those tags trigger.

    Common Mistakes

    • Activating before the test record.
    • Tagging many contacts without checking which published workflow the tag fires.

    15.2 Create a Funnel Variant

    Owner Operations, OperatorTime 1 daySystem Change log, landing page, Instantly, TantraSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A variant is how the funnel learns. Change too much at once and the result cannot be attributed. A variant with no spec and no control group teaches nothing, however well it performs.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Writes the variant spec and a launch checklist with every item and its state.
    What the Operator Does
    • Choose one or two levers. Approve the spec. Give the go.

    Every Step

    1. Write a variant spec in the change log with the id FV-<yyyymmdd>-<short-name>, the hypothesis, the audience, the title and body, the landing page, the email sequence, the offer, the tracking tags (utm_source=<channel>&utm_campaign=<variant id>), the volume, the dates, the success metric and the comparison control group.
    2. Change one or two levers against the control. More than that and the result cannot be attributed.
    3. Build the pieces as drafts or previews first (the landing-page variant, outreach template and automation cards).
    4. Present a launch checklist with each item and its state. Launch only after 'go'.
    5. After the event, record the result against the spec.

    Done When A recorded variant, run against a control, with a result in the log.

    The Lever Table

    LeverOptions todayEvidence
    AudienceGeography (UK first; the Netherlands, Switzerland, Singapore, France and Hong Kong are consistent losers; Germany excluded). Seniority (Head of at least as good as C-suite). Cold, warm re-invite or no-show remarketing. Fresh or recycled leads.The segment analysis in Part 1
    Invite titleV1 to V5, never renumbered. V2 is strongest. A new title becomes V6 when adopted.Part 4
    Invite bodyCalendar Outreach variations 1 to 5 in the Consolidated Document
    Landing pageThe current page, a second branded version, a new variant Worker, form fields, a bonus such as a Board ToolkitUntested: no attribution tags yet
    Email sequenceThe current three steps, older templates 1 to 4, a five-step shapeOnly the three-step has run
    Webinar titleThe current masterclass, or eleven alternatives in the Consolidated Document tab 'Titles for Webinar'Only one topic has run
    Offer and call to actionTier set, deposit or full payment, cohort dates, call or apply or career review, a Digital downsell
    Channel mix and volumeWaves, time slots, daily caps, the Instantly daily limitPart 4

    What Good Looks Like

    • Variants of the landing page deploy as a new Worker on a new route, never over the live hostname.

    Common Mistakes

    • A variant with no control group.

    15.3 Build a Landing Page Variant

    Owner OperationsTime 1 daySystem CloudflareSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    The live page is what every invite points to. A variant lets a new headline or form be tested without touching it.

    Every Step

    1. Build a new page from the copy of the current or second branded version. Keep the operator's host block, the six-step roadmap, the registration form posting to the same backend (so registrants still reach WebinarGeek and the Work Tracker), and the tracking-tag passthrough.
    2. Deploy as a new Worker on a new route, for example a path on the pro domain or a new subdomain. Never over the registration hostname or the dashboard.
    3. Test: open it, submit a test registration, confirm it reached WebinarGeek and the Registrants tab, and note the test entry for removal.
    4. Pointing calendar invites at the variant changes the wave brief (the location field), not the page.

    Done When A variant live on its own route, with a test registration that reached every destination.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The live page's source is held by the developer and the backend belongs to GrowthClub. Know who to ask.

    Common Mistakes

    • Deploying over the live route.

    15.4 Handle a GDPR Deletion Request

    Owner OperationsTime Same daySystem Sheets, Tantra, Instantly, GHLSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Suppression stops contact. Erasure removes data. They are not the same, and a person who has asked to be erased and is only suppressed has not had their request answered. Two requests have been open since the summer.

    Every Step

    1. Suppress the person or domain first (3.4).
    2. Remove the row from the Master Outreach Sheet tabs, the Work Tracker and any local file.
    3. Delete or anonymise the GHL contact, and remove them from WebinarGeek, according to the data policy.
    4. Send a reply to the person confirming what was done.
    5. Record the request, the date and the actions in the change log.
    6. Erasure itself is never done from the chat. It is a brief to operations.

    Done When Suppressed everywhere, erased from every store, and a reply sent and logged.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The reply is sent. A silent erasure still leaves an open request in the person's eyes.

    Common Mistakes

    • Treating a suppression as a deletion.

    15.5 Rotate a Key or a Shared Credential

    Owner OperationsTime 30 minSystem Secret storesSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Keys are rotated after every setup that involved a vendor, and any time one is pasted into a chat. A key that was shared once and never changed is an open door.

    Every Step

    1. List which system each key belongs to, and where it is stored.
    2. Create the new key in that system's own settings.
    3. Put it in the secret store (the Worker's secrets, or the local keys file). Never into a document, a repository or a chat.
    4. Run the tool's connection test (14.2) to prove the new key works.
    5. Revoke the old key. Record the date.

    Done When The new key works, the old one is revoked, and the date is recorded.

    What Good Looks Like

    • One key per tool. A shared admin key is a single point of failure.

    Common Mistakes

    • Revoking the old key before the new one is tested.

    15.6 Connect WebinarGeek and Keep the Connection Healthy

    Owner OperationsTime 30 minSystem WebinarGeekSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    Everything that registers people, reads attendance or links an invite to a broadcast goes through one WebinarGeek key. The key has quirks that have each broken a connection. This card is the connect runbook, for a new account, a new key or a repair. WebinarGeek is connected through the connector, Current for FINTECH today.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Tests the key and the webinar id by reading the webinar and its broadcasts through the connector, and reports exactly which one fails.
    What the Operator Does
    • Do the steps in WebinarGeek's own screen. Paste the key and the id where the connection asks for them. Tell Claude when the key changes.

    Every Step

    1. The API is off on a trial. On the 14-day trial, WebinarGeek support must switch the API on. Ask in the chat window.
    2. Know the limits. 10 requests a minute and 500 a day on a trial: enough for one webinar's setup and registrations, not for bulk work.
    3. Make the base webinar by hand. WebinarGeek's API has no way to create the base webinar. A person creates it (a live webinar, the same title, date and time as the registration page, 60 minutes). After that the connector can add broadcasts to it.
    4. Copy the key. Account, Integrations, API. There is one key for the whole account.
    5. A new key kills the old one. Clicking Generate API key switches the old key off, so every tool that used it stops until the new key is pasted everywhere: the connector, the Worker and the registration backend.
    6. Take the webinar id from the API reference icon next to Edit webinar, not from the address bar. The number in the address bar is the episode id.
    7. Never skip the confirmation email. The registration request has an option that skips it. Do not set it, or no confirmation email goes out. In plain words: do not suppress the confirmation email.
    8. Test. Claude reads the webinar and its broadcasts. A pass shows the webinar title and the next broadcast.

    Done When Claude reads the webinar and its next broadcast, and a test registration receives its confirmation email.

    ErrorWhat it meansFix
    401 UnauthorizedThe key was copied with a space or from an old screenCopy it again from Integrations, API
    Other tools stopped syncingSomeone generated a new key, which switched the old one offPaste the new key everywhere it was used
    Webinar not foundThe id came from the address bar, a broadcast or a registration pageUse the id from the API reference icon

    What Good Looks Like

    • The webinar id is recorded in one place, and the key's owner is named.

    Common Mistakes

    • Copying the number from the address bar.
    • Generating a new key to 'check' it, which silently breaks every other tool.

    15.7 Connect Zoom for the Mid-November Test

    Owner Operations, the operator decidesTime Half a day, then a 15-minute rehearsalSystem ZoomSafety Person

    Why It Matters

    A one-month test of Zoom against WebinarGeek is decided for the mid-November webinar. The Friday webinar stays on WebinarGeek. Zoom is Potential: nothing is connected yet. Run as a Pro meeting with registration, Zoom gives every person a personal join link and costs less than a Zoom Webinars licence for groups up to 100.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Once connected, would create the meeting with registration on, register each person and read attendance and the recording afterwards, through Zoom's API.
    • Today the connector has no Zoom tool, so one has to be added before Claude can do any of this.
    What the Operator Does
    • Switch on the account settings below, create the app inside Zoom, paste its credentials into the connection, run the rehearsal, and lock the room at the start of each session.

    Every Step

    1. Plan. Zoom Pro or above. A Pro room holds 100 people, and hosts and co-hosts count. A larger room needs the Large Meetings add-on.
    2. Set the account switches first. Account settings beat anything an app sets. In Zoom's Meeting settings: Meeting Passcode on; Embed passcode in invite link on (the passcode travels in each person's link, so nobody types it); Only authenticated participants can join off; Focus mode on, with Allow host to enable focus mode when scheduling; Request permission to unmute participants on; Co-host on; Cloud recording on. A greyed switch is locked for the whole account: change it in the account-level settings as the owner.
    3. Create the app. In the Zoom App Marketplace: Develop, Build App, Server-to-Server OAuth (an app that acts for the account without a person logging in). The account owner can build it.
    4. Add the 14 permissions (scopes), in plain words: create, update, read and list meetings (4); create and list polls (2); add and list registrants (2); read past meeting instances and past participants, which is how attendance is read (2); read users (2); read and list cloud recordings (2).
    5. Activate, then paste the Account ID, Client ID and Client Secret into the connection. Copy the Secret Token and save it before turning on Event Subscriptions, and tick 'All recordings have completed' so the replay link can follow the recording.
    6. Lock the room. No account setting stops people unmuting or starting video. At the start of each session open Security and untick Unmute Themselves and Start Video. Or ask Zoom Support once to switch on host mute control and participant video disable for the account.
    7. Co-hosts are made inside the meeting: Participants, hover a name, More, Make Co-Host. Alternative hosts set in advance must be licensed users on the account.
    8. Reminders and attendance. Zoom sends no reminder emails for meetings, so the funnel's own reminders must carry each person's personal link. Zoom has no attendance feed, so attended and no-show are read from the participant report after the session.
    9. Know the errors. Error 1001: registrants are refused because 'Only authenticated participants can join' is on. 429 when adding registrants: Zoom allows 3 registrations per person per day, so rehearse with a fresh email each time.

    Done When A 15-minute rehearsal passes: registered, joined from two devices, chat and a poll worked, the recording arrived and attendance showed.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The rehearsal uses a fresh email for every test registration.

    Common Mistakes

    • Trusting the app's room settings over the account's.
    • Rehearsing with one email over and over and hitting the 3 a day limit.

    15.8 SMS, AI Voice Calls and Analytics: What Can Be Added

    Owner The operator decides, operations buildsTime Per optionSystem Twilio, ElevenLabs or Vodex, Google AnalyticsSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Three extra tools can sit around the funnel. None is in use today, so each is marked Available or Potential. The numbers below are reference starting points, not FINTECH results. WhatsApp already runs through GHL and is not part of this card.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Would do the setup once access exists: build the sender, the call agent or the measurement, and read the results.
    • Writes the plan card for each, including opt-in wording.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide whether each is worth adding. Open the account, fund it and approve the business details. Only a person can add money or consent.

    Every Step

    1. SMS through Twilio. Upgrade from the trial and fund the balance (the reference says at least $20) before anything is bought. Create a Standard API key, never the main key. In the US and Canada a toll-free number needs verification, which takes 3 to 5 business days, and unverified toll-free traffic is blocked. Only people who tick an SMS box get texts, and STOP unsubscribes them everywhere. One text is 160 plain characters, or 70 with an emoji. India needs a registration Twilio cannot do, so use WhatsApp or email there.
    2. SMS is for time-critical moments only, such as doors opening or a live session, never every message.
    3. AI voice call at go-live (optional). When the session starts, an AI voice calls only people who ticked a call box, once each, in under 30 seconds. It uses ElevenLabs or Vodex with the account's own phone number, never a bought one. Automated calls are regulated, so the box is never pre-ticked. No call is a complete answer.
    4. Google Analytics (GA4). Free. An Administrator adds the connection's service account as an Editor at account level, and proves the website is owned by adding a DNS record. Registrations and booked calls are then counted as key events, so registrations by source sit beside the other dashboard numbers.
    5. FINTECH today: there is no analytics tag on the landing pages, and visits do not yet show on each contact. Both are open actions (28.4).

    Done When Each option has a recorded decision: adopt, test, or not now.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Each option is added one at a time, after the plan card.

    Common Mistakes

    • Planning to call from a Twilio number: Twilio is for texts only here.
    • Treating the call as a broadcast to every registrant.

    15.9 The Automation Register: What Is Proven, Failing or Not Built

    Owner Claude, operationsTime 15 min a monthSystem GHL, Worker, sheet automationsSafety Read

    Why It Matters

    The funnel is a chain of automations. Some are proven, one fails silently, and some have never been built. A register keeps that honest, so nobody assumes a step exists. Statuses are as of 14 October and need re-reading before quoting.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Re-reads workflow names and status through the connector each month and updates the register.
    • Flags any automation that fails without an alert.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide which 'not built' items are worth building, in value order.

    Every Step

    1. Read the register below. Click each stage for its trigger and status.
    2. Before any automation is trusted, test it with two contacts: one with a phone number and one without. The first should get both the email and the WhatsApp journey. The second should get email only. Read each contact's tags and messages afterwards.
    3. Keep failures visible. A guard that exits silently needs an alert or a fallback branch.
    4. Mark each item: Proven means it has run for real people. Failing silently means it can exit with no alert. Not built means no workflow exists.
    5. Re-read before quoting. Workflow status drifts.

    Done When Every automation in the chain has a status, an owner and a last-checked date.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Nobody assumes a 'not built' step is running.

    Common Mistakes

    • Assuming WhatsApp follow-up exists. It does not.
    • Assuming a GHL unsubscribe stops cold email. It does not.

    15.10 The CRM Rules That Keep the Chain Intact

    Owner OperationsTime Standing rulesSystem GHL, WorkerSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Three small rules protect every automation that keys off a stage, a tag or an event. Breaking any of them fails silently: nothing errors, the automation simply stops matching.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Checks the rules before drafting any automation spec or tagging plan, and names any tag that does not exist yet.
    What the Operator Does
    • Create each tag in GHL before anything writes it. Never rename a stage or tag in place.

    Every Step

    1. Never rename a stage, tag or workflow. Name it once, write it down and leave it. Everything keys off the exact name, and a workflow check matches the exact name too. If a name must change, create the new one and move over deliberately.
    2. Tags exist before use. Create the tag in GHL, then use it. An automation that writes a tag that does not exist can fail without a message. Custom fields must exist before the first test submission for the same reason.
    3. Dedupe webhook events. A tool may send the same event twice, or late. Read the state the event describes, not the event name, so a repeat gives the same result and cannot create a second record or a second send.
    4. One owner per name. Use only the current tag names. Never filter on a legacy duplicate.

    Done When Every tag and stage in use has one fixed name, exists before use, and survives a repeated event.

    What Good Looks Like

    • A repeated webhook leaves the contact exactly as it was.

    Common Mistakes

    • Renaming a tag mid-cohort, so older people no longer match.
    • Writing a tag that was never created.

    20.1 How to Prepare a New Webinar

    Owner OperatorTime Half a daySystem WebinarGeek, outreach sheet, landing pageSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Everything the next cycle depends on is set once, in order, so nothing is changed after people have been sent the date.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the cohort calendar and the live state.
    • Drafts the page copy, banner text and deck changes.
    • Shows the plan card before anything is created.
    What the Operator Does
    • Pick the date.
    • Say go on the plan card.
    • Sign off the checklist.

    Before You Begin

    • The date is decided and the cohort it feeds is known.
    • Access to WebinarGeek, the outreach sheet and the landing page project.

    Verify

    Ask Claude to read the live state and list where the date appears. Every place matches.

    Rollback

    Nothing has reached people yet, so any step can be redone. If the broadcast is wrong, create a new one and leave the old one unused.

    Every Step

    1. Pick the date from the cohort calendar (2.1).
    2. Create the broadcast on the existing webinar and the sheet tab (2.2).
    3. Update page copy, banners and the deck (2.3).
    4. Check the landing page, the replay and the emails (2.4).
    5. Repoint the event configuration (2.5).
    6. Run the new-event checklist (26.5).

    Done When Every item on the new-event checklist is ticked and the plan card matches what exists.

    In order: date, broadcast, sheet tab, copy, checks.

    A one-off Zoom test (8.4) or a multi-day format (13.6).

    • The date appears the same everywhere: page, emails, deck, sequence.

    20.2 How to Build and Clean a Lead List

    Owner Operator, operationsTime 1 to 2 hoursSystem Apollo, cleaning rules, outreach sheetSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A list is only as safe as the checks it passed. Cleaning is the cheapest place to prevent a damaged domain.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the pool size and shows what is left.
    • Applies the cleaning rules and reports every removal and why.
    • Shows how each reply is classified before anything is blocked.
    What the Operator Does
    • Decide whether to buy.
    • Buy and export in Apollo.
    • Approve the cleaned list.

    Before You Begin

    • A written persona and the exclusion sources, current.
    • Budget approval if a purchase is planned.

    Verify

    The removal report names each rule and its count, and a ten-row sample of removed rows looks right.

    Rollback

    Cleaning writes new files, so delete the output and rerun. A purchase cannot be undone.

    Every Step

    1. Check whether the pool is big enough (3.1).
    2. Decide whether to buy (3.2).
    3. Clean the list (3.3).
    4. Run the suppression sweep (3.4).
    5. Load the tab (3.5).

    Done When The tab is loaded, the removal report was read and the suppression list is current.

    What
    A pool of safe, new people for the next wave.
    How
    Check size, decide on a purchase, clean, sweep suppressions, load.
    With what
    Apollo, the cleaning rules, the suppression list, the outreach sheet.
    What else
    Reuse of the owned pool at lower touch counts, or a different data source (Part 18).

    What Good Looks Like

    • The removal report names every group removed and how many.

    Common Mistakes

    • Cleaning against a stale exclusion source, which re-contacts people who already attended.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    SymptomLikely causeWhat to do
    Most rows are off-personaA raw bought list can be mostly non-financialFilter by industry first and read the removal report
    Names look swappedSome lists store first and last names reversedCross-check the name against the email before trusting it
    Another business's contacts appearBought lists can carry rows that belong elsewhereStrip them and flag the source

    20.13 How to Change the Date of a Broadcast

    Owner OperatorTime 30 minSystem WebinarGeek, landing page, Instantly, CRMSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A broadcast date can only be changed in WebinarGeek's own screen, and the reminder emails do not move with it. Without this checklist, people get reminders for the wrong time.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Reads the broadcast and lists every place that carries the old date.
    • Drafts the correction notice.
    • Checks the new schedule against the broadcast afterwards.
    What the Operator Does
    • Change the date in WebinarGeek's own screen.
    • Cancel and reschedule each reminder email.
    • Release the notice.

    Before You Begin

    • Everyone already invited is known.

    Verify

    All pages, emails and the broadcast show the same date.

    Rollback

    Set the date back; reminders already sent stay sent.

    Every Step

    1. Decide the new date and time, in the audience's time zone.
    2. Ask Claude to list everything that carries the old date. Read the plan card.
    3. In WebinarGeek, open Edit webinar, General, Date and time, Edit, Edit time, then Save. Open it again to check.
    4. In every reminder email, click Cancel planned emails and plan each one again. Send a test copy of each to a team mailbox.
    5. Update the landing page (6.3), the cold-email sequence (4.3) and the invitation text for later waves.
    6. Check the WhatsApp reminders follow the new broadcast date (7.2).
    7. If invitations already went out, ask Claude to draft a short correction. Sending it is Send now.
    8. Read the registrations again to confirm nobody lost a link.

    Done When The reopened broadcast shows the new date, every reminder shows its new schedule and every copy of the date agrees.

    What
    A new date that every person and every message agrees on.
    How
    Change it by hand, then reschedule every reminder and every copy of the date.
    With what
    WebinarGeek's screen, the landing page, the cold-email sequence, the CRM, Claude.
    What else
    A smaller notice to people who already received the old date.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Reference starting point: test the reminders by moving a test broadcast to about an hour ahead and seeing the one-hour reminder fire.

    Common Mistakes

    • Changing only the broadcast and leaving the reminders on their old times.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    SymptomLikely causeWhat to do
    Reminders still go at the old timeReminder emails do not move with the broadcastOpen each one, cancel planned emails and plan them again
    The date cannot be changed from chatEditing a broadcast is not possible through the connectorA person does it in WebinarGeek; Claude checks the result
    Invited people still have the old timeCalendar invitations already sent keep the old timeSend a correction note (Send now) and say so in the next wave

    Full detail: 2.2, 7.1, 7.2, 6.3

    20.14 How to Tag Test Contacts

    Owner OperatorTime 20 minSystem CRM, landing pageSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A test that is counted as a result, or a test contact that receives a real campaign, spoils both the numbers and the sending. One clear tag keeps tests apart.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Finds the contact and adds the tag after a plan card.
    • Checks whether the dashboard and the sheet exclude it, and says plainly if they do not.
    What the Operator Does
    • Register a test address.
    • Say go on the plan card.

    Before You Begin

    • A list of test contacts, so real people are never tagged.

    Verify

    The test contact carries the tag and fires only the intended workflow.

    Rollback

    Remove the tag.

    Every Step

    1. Use a test address the team controls, such as a plus address on a team mailbox.
    2. Register it through the landing page like a real person.
    3. Ask Claude to find the contact and add one tag, "test". Read the plan card first: some tags start workflows (7.3).
    4. Walk it through the confirmation, the reminders and the WhatsApp reply.
    5. Ask Claude to confirm the dashboard and the outreach sheet do not count it. They are expected to filter it; verify on the next test.
    6. Keep the contact for the next test. Keep the tag in the tag list (7.4).

    Done When The test contact is tagged, received every message and is not in any result.

    What
    A test person who never counts as a result.
    How
    Register a test address the team owns, tag it, walk it through, then check the counts.
    With what
    The landing page, the CRM tag tool, the dashboard, Claude.
    What else
    A full rehearsal of every reminder on a test broadcast.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Every test uses a contact that carries the tag.

    Common Mistakes

    • Testing with a real lead's address, which sends them real messages.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    SymptomLikely causeWhat to do
    A real campaign reached the test contactThe tag is not in the exclusion list yetAdd it to the exclusions and suppress the address
    Test registrations appear in the resultsThe dashboard may not filter the tagAsk Claude to check the count, subtract it and record the gap
    Tagging started a workflow unexpectedlySome tags start workflowsRead the workflow list first (7.3)

    Full detail: 6.1, 7.3, 7.4

    20.16 How to Connect WebinarGeek

    Owner Technical ownerTime 30 minSystem WebinarGeek, connectorSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Every registration, reminder and attendance figure depends on this connection. A wrong key or the wrong id fails quietly.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Lists webinars and broadcasts to prove the connection.
    • Registers a test address and checks the confirmation email.
    What the Operator Does
    • Switch on the API and copy the key.
    • Store the key where only the technical owner can reach it.
    • Copy the webinar id.

    Before You Begin

    • An account with an API key held in the secret store.

    Verify

    List the webinar and its broadcasts through the connector.

    Rollback

    Rotate or remove the key.

    Every Step

    1. Create the account. On the 14 day trial the API is off until WebinarGeek support switches it on; ask in the chat window.
    2. Know the limits: 10 requests a minute and 500 a day. That is enough for one webinar's set-up and registrations.
    3. Make the base webinar by hand. Every later broadcast is made on it.
    4. Open Account, Integrations, API and copy the key. Keep it out of chat and out of shared files.
    5. Get the webinar id from the API reference icon next to Edit webinar. The number in the address bar is the episode id.
    6. Ask Claude to list the webinars and the broadcasts. That proves the link (Read).
    7. Register a test address the team owns. Never switch off the confirmation email when registering through the API.

    Done When Claude lists the right webinar and a test registration receives its confirmation.

    What
    A working link between Claude and the webinar platform.
    How
    Switch the API on, copy the key and the webinar id, prove it with a read.
    With what
    WebinarGeek's integrations screen, the FINTECH connector, Claude.
    What else
    A second platform for a test (8.4).

    What Good Looks Like

    • One key, held by one person.

    Common Mistakes

    • Generating a new key without telling the rest. A new key switches off the old one, so everything using it stops.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    SymptomLikely causeWhat to do
    401 UnauthorizedThe key was copied with a space or from an old screenCopy it again from Integrations, API
    Other tools stopped syncingSomeone generated a new keyPaste the new key everywhere the old one was used
    Webinar not foundThe episode id was used instead of the webinar idTake the id from the API reference icon

    20.17 How to Connect and Test Zoom

    Owner Technical owner, operatorTime Half a day, then a test weekSystem Zoom, WebinarGeek, CRMSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    A Zoom test is planned for the mid-November webinar (8.4). Zoom is Potential until the test passes. Connecting it takes care, and a failed room is costly.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Creates the test session and registers test contacts.
    • Reads participants after the session and compares them to registrants.
    What the Operator Does
    • Check the account settings and build the private app.
    • Lock the room at the start of each session.

    Before You Begin

    • A paid plan that supports webinars, and the permission count read.

    Verify

    A test registration receives a join link and a reminder.

    Rollback

    Disable the connection; nothing else depends on it yet.

    Every Step

    1. Check the account settings first: passcode on and inside the link, only authenticated participants off, focus mode on, permission to unmute on, co-host and cloud recording on. A greyed switch is locked for the whole account.
    2. In the Zoom marketplace build a Server-to-Server app with only the permissions on the card.
    3. Store the account ID, client ID and secret safely. Activate the app.
    4. Subscribe to the recording-complete event once the receiving address exists.
    5. A week before the event, create a test session, register two test contacts and join from two devices.
    6. Plan for the 100 person cap. It counts the host and co-hosts.
    7. Remember Zoom meetings send no reminder emails. The funnel sends all of them. Zoom Webinars do send reminders.
    8. After the session, compare the participant list with the registrants.

    Done When A test session was created, two test contacts joined, the replay link arrived and the room locked correctly.

    What
    A Zoom room that Claude can create sessions in and read attendance from.
    How
    Check account settings, create a private app, test a week before, lock the room at the start.
    With what
    Zoom's marketplace and settings, the registration page, the CRM, Claude.
    What else
    Zoom Webinars, which do send reminders, or a larger room.

    What Good Looks Like

    • The room is locked in two clicks at the start of every session.

    • Assuming the account settings cannot override the app. They can.

    20.15 How to Set Up a Meta Ads Test

    Owner Operator, OperatorTime 1 day to set up, then a weekSystem Meta Ads Manager, landing page, analyticsSafety Send now

    Why It Matters

    FINTECH does not run Meta ads today. This is the smallest honest test: two ads, one small budget, one number to judge them by. It stays Potential until the first test is approved.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Works out the target and drafts two ads and tagged links.
    • Reads results weekly and recommends scale, hold or pause.
    What the Operator Does
    • Create the account and payment method.
    • Build and switch on the campaign.
    • Approve every spend.

    Before You Begin

    • A spend cap and approval.

    Verify

    A test registration shows in the ads tool and in analytics.

    Rollback

    Pause the ad set; spend already incurred stays.

    Every Step

    1. Mark the registration as the conversion in Google Analytics and in Meta (6.4).
    2. Install the Meta tracking code and see a page view in Test events.
    3. Start the retargeting pool on day one: visitors minus registrants. Add a lookalike once 100 people have registered (reference starting point).
    4. Write two ads that differ only in angle. Tag each link with the source, medium, campaign and content.
    5. Set the target cost per registration: the most one buyer is worth, times the show rate, times the close rate. The reference playbook's example of 300 x 40% x 10% = 12 is a teaching model, not a FINTECH figure; use FINTECH's own numbers.
    6. Launch on one small fixed daily budget. Change one thing at a time.
    7. Test before trusting: view on a phone and make a real test registration that appears in Meta and Google Analytics.
    8. Leave the ads alone for several days, then judge each by cost per registration.

    Done When A test registration appears in both Meta and Google Analytics, and both ads are running with tagged links.

    What
    A judged answer to whether paid Meta ads bring registrations at an acceptable cost.
    How
    Track the registration first, then test two ads that differ only in angle.
    With what
    Meta Ads Manager, the landing page, Google Analytics, Claude.
    What else
    Retargeting to visitors, a lookalike, Google Ads.

    What Good Looks Like

    • Scale at or under the target by adding budget, not new variables. Pause an ad that spends three times the target with no registrations. In between, change exactly one thing.

    Common Mistakes

    • Judging ads by clicks. Launching before a test registration shows up.

    Registrants are being paid for twiceThe pool does not exclude themExclude the registration event from the pool

    A booked call that is missed is still a warm lead. A fixed sequence brings most of them back and never mixes with the webinar no-show message. Nothing here runs today; it is Potential.

    20.22 How to Do the Monthly Cost-Per-Buyer Rebalance

    Owner Operator, OperatorTime 1 hour each monthSystem Cost register, CRM, Google AnalyticsSafety Go

    Why It Matters

    Clicks and registrations flatter every channel. Cost per buyer is the only fair comparison, and it is Potential until registrations carry their source.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Totals spend, counts buyers by source and ranks the channels.

    • Decide where the money moves.

    1. Gather the month's spend for each channel from the cost register (16.3).
    2. Count buyers for each channel by the source on their registration. Today the source field on registrations is empty, so this needs the page to capture it first (6.2).
    3. Divide spend by buyers for each channel.
    4. Rank the channels.
    5. Move budget from the dearest toward the cheapest, keeping total spend the same.
    6. Leave a small test budget on each channel.
    7. Record the decision (10.3).

    20.12 How to Troubleshoot Common Failures

    Why It Matters

    Most failures in this stack have been seen before. The cost of a wrong guess is a duplicate send or a blocked domain, so find the symptom first.

    How It Works

    What Claude Does
    • Re-reads live state before saying what is wrong.
    • Matches the symptom to the table and proposes the fix as a plan card.
    What the Operator Does
    • Describe the symptom in plain words.

    Every Step

    1. Find the symptom in the table.
    2. Re-read live state before acting (a claim about a live system is true only in the turn it was read).
    3. Follow the fix. If it is not listed, stop and ask for a plan card.

    What
    A named cause and a safe fix.
    How
    Find the symptom, re-read, fix, re-read.
    With what

    What else
    Add each new failure to the table so it is only learned once.
